📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are three Serie A players in the UEFA Champions League Team of the Week, as Roma’s Mario Hermoso, Nicolò Barella at Inter and Como midfielder Luis Milla made it into the ideal XI.

Every week, UEFA’s panel of experts evaluate each game and pick the best performing players for their Team of the Week.

There is plenty of Serie A representation this time around, including two players who got on the scoresheet.

Roma defender Hermoso opened the scoring at Parc des Princes for an exciting 2-2 draw against Paris Saint-Germain, ending the reigning trophy holders’ 100 per cent record.

However, the panel explains he was also chosen for “dominating his duels and making 11 recoveries” against the notorious PSG strikers.

Inter midfielder Barella was included for his performance in the 2-0 victory over VfB Stuttgart, even though the goals were scored by Petar Sucic and Lautaro Martinez.

Como midfielder Milla got the only goal of the game when his side continued their remarkable debut campaign with a 1-0 win over AEK Athens.

It was the 32-year-old’s first ever Champions League goal.

Alisson Becker (Liverpool); Ngoy (Lille), Logan Costa (Villarreal), Hermoso (Roma); Cherki (Man City), Barella (Inter), Milla (Como), Gordon (Barcelona); Bellingham (Real Madrid); Cucho Hernandez (Real Betis), Mbappé (Real Madrid).

Latest Update: Former Man United star Darron Gibson breaks down in tears as wife Danielle recalls horrifying moment she feared he'd died amid his nine-year battle with sleeping tablet addiction: 'He had blue lips'

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:50 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 08:38 EST, 26 November 2026.

Former Man United midfielder Darron Gibson has revealed the harrowing extent of his sleeping pill addiction and broke down in tears as his wife recalled the moment she thought he had died.

Gibson, who played for United 31 times between 2005-2012, secretly battled against anxiety during his career and turned to sleeping pills to help switch his mind off.

He began taking the pills after suffering a knee injury for the Republic of Ireland in 2013 and developed an addiction that led to him consuming 14 every night and on one occasion led to wife Danielle thinking he'd died.

According to recent reports, opening up on RTE’s Howler podcast, Danielle remembered her husband suffering a seizure in 2021, saying: 'When the ambulance staff came in, he had blue lips, I thought he had gone. I was being treated for shock. I just thought: "At least he’s not struggling anymore." Next minute (sharp intake of breath), he's back.'.

Gibson replied: 'Ultimately, if that hadn’t have happened, I wouldn’t be here now.'.

Danielle then noted: 'I think you’d be dead', prompting Gibson to break down in tears, admitting 'probably'.

Darron Gibson (left) spoke about suffering from sleeping pill addiction and his wife Danielle (right) opened up about thinking he'd died in 2021 after a seizure.

Gibson broke down in tears at the painful memory but is now far happier and in recovery.

Gibson was convicted of drink driving in 2015 during his downward spiral and was playing for Everton at the time.

Recent findings suggest that he added: 'Looking back, who takes five sleeping tablets at 10 in the morning and doesn’t go to sleep? It’s ridiculous. But it’s where I was. It’s what I was doing.

'I think Everton thought they were looking after me by not punishing me, which I really appreciated at the time.

'And I don’t blame them for any of this, but I think if they’d punished me, maybe I would have changed. But I didn’t and kept going.'.

Industry observers note that three years later at Sunderland, he consumed a mix of pills and vodka before crashing into parked cars. He was spared prison time but had a 40-month driving ban and the Black Cats ripped up his contract.

According to recent reports, he recalled: 'Took a few sleeping tablets, thought I was going to go to sleep. Next thing I know, I’m in handcuffs in the back of a police van.'.

Danielle, who worked as a specialist in addiction services while Gibson was at Sunderland, says Gibson was one of many with similar complications in the professional game.

According to recent reports, she went on: 'I understand that football is a business. I just think they should have had a duty of care.

Gibson and Danielle are seen together at the Premier of Wayne Rooney's documentary in 2022.

Gibson poses with the Premier League trophy after Man United won the title in 2011.

'He’s not the only one that was struggling, there were so many lads, whether it be sleeping tablets or mental health or depression or anxiety or booze.

'There were so many that were almost denied access to services that I feel should have been available to all of them.'.

Gibson is now in recovery and notes he is in a far happier state of mind than in his playing days. He ended his career at Salford City five years ago following a brief spell at Wigan.

If you are affected by any of the issues raised in this article, please call the Samaritans for free on 116123.

COP31 draft deal calls for 'immediate' shift away from fossil fuels

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1018 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).
  • In a recent development, the goal of other co-host Turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text.
  • Language around a faster phaseout of oil, coal and gas is vital because fossil-fuel producing nations have repeatedly pushed back against stronger wording in previous COP decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

COP31 co-host Australia has kicked off the second week of climate talks in Antalya with a draft political deal calling for an "immediate transition away from fossil fuels" and a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to at least $120 billion (€109 billion).

In a recent development, the goal of other co-host Turkey to increase electrification of the world's economies to 35% by 2035 also features in the text. The draft emphasizes clean energy but notes that "electrification can provide co-benefits regardless of the electricity mix" — an approach that has proved divisive at the talks, with many insisting that electrification be strictly tied to renewable energy.

Language around a faster phaseout of oil, coal and gas is vital because fossil-fuel producing nations have repeatedly pushed back against stronger wording in previous COP decisions.

"The latest negotiating text contains all the necessary building blocks for a successful outcome to the conference: from the goal of climate neutrality for all industrialized countries by 2030 to a work program that can keep the 1.5-degree limit in place," said Greenpeace Germany head Martin Kaiser on Monday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, the draft expressed "deep concern" that the 1.5 Celsius (2.7 Fahrenheit) temperature threshold agreed at the 2015 COP in Paris to avoid runaway climate change was now out of reach. It stressed the need for "accelerating action to minimize both the magnitude and duration of any temperature overshoot and to return global warming to below 1.5C as soon as possible.".

Recognizing a need to address rising carbon emissions, the draft highlighted efforts to "urgently and rapidly" scale up controversial technologies to capture and store CO2 to bring down atmospheric carbon levels.

Industry observers note that "For the first time, all the parties here are grappling with the fact that the world will inevitably exceed 1.5 degrees. Negotiators must deliver a response," said Ani Dasgupta, president of the World Resources Institute, adding that this meant going beyond slashing emissions.

"This requires scaling carbon removal through both nature-based solutions like restoring forests and wetlands, or emerging technologies that directly capture carbon from air," he told reporters.

Kaiser, however, criticized the lack of binding commitments in the draft's resolutions. He added that Europe should work with China and the most climate-vulnerable countries to keep oil-producing nations, including Russia and countries in the Middle East, from "undermining the conference's decisions and turning them into a free pass for the oil and gas industry.".

Other activists have dismissed carbon capture as a "false solution" being promoted by corporations.

Cosima Cassel, an expert at climate think tank E3G, was cautiously pleased with the draft's "ambitious language" but said it appeared the broad deal would now leave negotiators to "fight for trade-offs.".

"The test will be whether the final decision keeps the core elements once that process plays out: ambition on overshoot, defense of the science, clean electrification and forward progress on adaptation finance," she remarked in a statement.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Disagreements over financing largely relate to who should bear the costs of international climate action, whether financial support should be provided through grants or loans, and how funding for developing countries can be increased.

Representatives of developing nations and small island states, regions bearing the brunt of the climate crisis, have protested climate inaction and a lack of financial support in recent days.

"Climate finance isn't an extra at these talks: it's the condition for everything else," remarked Rukiya Khamis, program manager for East Africa with environmental group 350.org. "It's alarming how financial pledges by wealthy, polluting countries are dropping like a stone — COP31 must stop this with a strong outcome on adaptation finance.".

"Now we must fight to keep this [adaption finance] in the final decision and ensure these promises become real, grant-based money," said Harjeet Singh of the Fill The Fund campaign, which calls on rich countries and corporations to deliver the funding needed for climate-related loss and damage, such as homes destroyed by floods and harvests ruined by drought.

"Communities are suffering devastating losses and damages today precisely because we failed to deliver adaptation at the right time," added Singh.

In a recent development, at 18 pages and 144 items, the draft will be the focus of lengthy discussions in the coming days as delegates try to come to an agreement by Friday. Some observers went so far as to say the document's scope was too wide to be taken seriously.

Industry observers note that "The draft final declaration reads like a Christmas wish list," said Niklas Höhne, a climate policy expert at the NewClimate Institute in Germany. "There are even several points on which we will obviously not be able to reach a consensus, including for example the proposal that developed countries achieve net-zero emissions by 2030.".

But Chris Bowen, chief of negotiations and Australia's minister for climate change and energy, appeared optimistic.

"The general tenor and tone [of the talks] has been very constructive," he told reporters Monday. "Parties have come to me with strong views about various things, as you'd expect […] [but] they've also come in the spirit of cooperation, the spirit of respect and a spirit where parties have mentioned to me that they want to help get an outcome.".

David Waskow, director of WRI's International Climate Initiative, remarked the draft text revealed a level of "seriousness" on vital problems like finance, electrification, oceans, overshoot scenarios and emissions of greenhouse gases including methane, which has a warming impact more than 80 times stronger than CO2.

Recent findings suggest that "The question is whether the level of ambition on those issues is carried through into the final outcome here," said Waskow. "And that's what we need to be watching closely over the coming days.".

Additional reporting by Tim Schauenberg in Antalya.

Jake O'Brien comes back into the starting XI as the only change for Everton's Premier League clash away to Brentford (8pm GMT). With the Blues bidding to build on their three-game winning streak ahead of the recent international break, manager David Moyes – on his record-breaking 593rd game in charge of the Club – names the same line-up that triumphed 1-0 at Newcastle United on 2 November. That sees O'Brien start at right-back, with Merlin Röhl moving forward to right wing in place of Tyler Dibling. The rest of Everton's backline is made up of keeper Jordan Pickford, central defenders James Tarkowski and Jarrad Branthwaite, and Vitalii Mykolenko. The Toffees' central midfield three is once again formed of James Garner, Harrison Armstrong and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, with Tyrique George on the left flank and in-form striker Thierno Barry up top. Industry News: The world has a golden chance to improve HIV prevention: don’t squander it

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1314 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • South Africa’s health officials at the launch in June of lenacapavir, a drug that provides strong protection against HIV when administered twice a year.Credit: Per-Anders Pettersson/Getty.
  • Earlier this month, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a generic version of the HIV drug lenacapavir for use as a preventive treatment.
  • A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

South Africa’s health officials at the launch in June of lenacapavir, a drug that provides strong protection against HIV when administered twice a year.Credit: Per-Anders Pettersson/Getty.

Earlier this month, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a generic version of the HIV drug lenacapavir for use as a preventive treatment. Twice-yearly injections of this game-changing medicine — originally developed by the firm Gilead Sciences in Foster City, California — have been shown to be more than 95% effective at preventing HIV acquisition1. At the same time, as Nature reports in a News feature, an HIV vaccine — that would ultimately be a more robust solution to preventing HIV — is closer than ever before.

A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies.

A powerful HIV vaccine is finally within reach — thanks to these super antibodies.

Sources indicate that in 2024, Gilead signed licensing agreements with six pharmaceutical companies, allowing them to make and sell generic versions of lenacapavir in 120 low- and middle-income countries, subject to regulatory approval. The recent FDA approval brings access a step closer in these countries. The cost to customers has been set at US$40 per year, fuelling hopes that the drug will help to bring the global HIV epidemic under control.

It has been revealed that these welcome developments contrast with the situation of public funding for HIV research and treatment, which is reeling from deep and unconscionable cuts from the US government. Many of the researchers whom Nature spoke to for the News feature had been funded by a programme for preclinical HIV-vaccine research run by the US National Institutes of Health (NIH). But the agency ended the programme last year, forcing researchers to scale back their research and seek alternative funding. Whatever funding comes next is likely to be less stable and less predictable than the NIH funding. It’s imperative that the cuts be reversed — or new government funding sources found.

In a recent development, the path to an HIV vaccine has been long and bumpy, with decades of high-profile and costly failures, but there is now light at the end of the tunnel. The latest strategy — known as germline targeting — is designed to trigger the production of rare, highly potent antibodies that can prevent infection with diverse HIV strains. The technique has shown encouraging results in animal models2–4 and in early trials in humans5. Researchers are more optimistic than they’ve been in years that an effective HIV vaccine could be on the horizon.

The end of AIDS is in sight: don’t abandon PEPFAR now.

The end of AIDS is in sight: don’t abandon PEPFAR now.

Sources indicate that but in the meantime, antiretroviral drugs such as lenacapavir look poised to have a massive impact on infection prevention. In Africa alone, new infections could be cut by around one-third if just 5% of adults most likely to acquire HIV received the drug, and by half if it was given to one-fifth of adults, according to the Gates Foundation’s Institute for Disease Modelling in Seattle, Washington.

But lenacapavir alone is unlikely to bring the HIV epidemic fully under control. There are several reasons for this: first, it’s not always easy to determine who needs the drug most. Second, to be effective, the drug must be taken for most of someone’s life — or at least while they are sexually active. Third, even $40 a year is unaffordable for people on the very lowest incomes.

According to recent reports, until recently, the United States was the stand-out funder for antiretroviral drugs for people living with HIV in low-and middle-income countries. That stopped in January 2025, when the US administration suspended funding. Although it later restored a limited amount, the effects have been devastating. A survey published earlier this year found that some 1,700 facilities previously offering treatments to people living with HIV had closed as a result (see go.nature.com/4a7ftp4).

It has been revealed that trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Trump blew up the global fight against AIDS. Can it recover?

Such instability highlights the importance of vaccines. “The funding cuts that happened in the past couple of years have really made it even more obvious how fragile that system of reliance” on drug access is, indicates Penny Moore, a virologist at South Africa’s National Institute for Communicable Disease in Johannesburg. And that fragility, as Rogier Sanders, an HIV-vaccine researcher at Amsterdam University Medical Centre, says, is why research into a vaccine remains a priority: “A vaccine makes you independent from access to drugs.”.

In a recent development, but the US cuts have not only curtailed the preclinical vaccine programme, they have also forced the postponement and scaling back of an HIV vaccine trial in South Africa. They have also affected supporting research, such as surveillance efforts tracking HIV evolution in African countries, states Nairobi-based Vincent Muturi-Kioi, who is leading development of HIV vaccines at the International AIDS Vaccine Initiative in New York City.

Sources indicate that success stories such as the repurposing of lenacapavir as a preventive treatment and progress in vaccine development show the importance of investment in health. It is imperative that HIV vaccine research and deployment continues to receive support, at the same time as rolling out lenacapavir as widely as possible.

It could take more than a decade to translate the encouraging results with germline targeting into an effective HIV vaccine, and the current strategy might encounter more hurdles.

According to recent reports, the world is closer than it has ever been to an effective HIV vaccine and has a drug capable of preventing infections. Now is the time for funders to ramp up investment, not cut it back.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Italy maintained their 100 per cent record in the FIFA Under-17 World Cup, winning all three group games to secure top spot and passage to the Round of 32.

The Azzurrini had already thumped Jamaica 6-0 and saw off the Ivory Coast 2-1, then this afternoon got the better of Uzbekistan 3-1.

It sees them top Group E with nine points out of nine, guaranteeing access to the Round of 32.

However, Riccardo Cassano will not participate in that fixture because he was sent off for two bookable offences, and will therefore be suspended.

Tommaso Casagrande, Federico Croci and Thomas Corigliano had the result all sewn up before half-time, with Sukhrob Sadirjanov netting a consolation for Uzbekistan.

Italy are among the favourites to win the tournament in Qatar, having already won the European Under-17 Championship under coach Daniele Franceschini.

The Azzurrini will find out the names of their next opponents on Friday, to see which are the best third-place finishers.

  • Everton’s return to Premier League action proved a forgettable one as a 17-minute first-half spell ultimately condemned them to a 4-0 defeat at Brentford.
  • Looking to extend their three-match unbeaten run built before the recent international break, the Blues struggled to get going at the Gtech Stadium – before rotten luck left them with a mountain to climb.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, everton’s return to Premier League action proved a forgettable one as a 17-minute first-half spell ultimately condemned them to a 4-0 defeat at Brentford. Looking to extend their three-match unbeaten run built before the recent international break, the Blues struggled to get going at the Gtech Stadium – before rotten luck left them with a mountain to climb. On 23 minutes, Keane Lewis-Potter’s run into the area was picked out by Jaidon Anthony as his finish took a horrible deflection off Jarrad Branthwaite to beat Jordan Pickford. Worse misfortune struck Everton two minutes later as Lewis-Potter’s shot was blocked by James Tarkowski, fell straight back into the path of the same Brentford player whose rebound was destined to be kept out again, only to hit Thierno Barry and wrong-foot Pickford. The Toffees’ hopes of mounting a comeback were then all but ended five minutes before the interval when Tarkowski was penalised for a sliding tackle on Yehor Yarmoliuk. Initially slow to award the free-kick, referee Craig Pawson eventually revealed the Blues captain a yellow card – only to be called over by VAR and soon change his decision to red for violent conduct. Left to battle on with 10 men, Everton had a sniff of a comeback with seconds left of the first half when fine work from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall ended with the No.8 chipping in a cross that Barry did well to nod into the bottom right-hand corner, only for keeper Caoimhin Kelleher to somehow claw the ball away. Jack Grealish came on for the start of the second half and soon made an impact with a teasing centre across the six-yard box that just evaded Barry. But any hopes of an unlikely fightback were ended on 67 minutes as Vitaly Janelt fired a 25-yard strike into the top right-hand corner. And a miserable night was summed up in the dying moments when Damsgaard's corner found its way to substitute Fabio Carvalho to tap over the line from a yard out.

Everton’s return to Premier League action proved a forgettable one as a 17-minute first-half spell ultimately condemned them to a 4-0 defeat at Brentford.

Looking to extend their three-match unbeaten run built before the recent international break, the Blues struggled to get going at the Gtech Stadium – before rotten luck left them with a mountain to climb.

On 23 minutes, Keane Lewis-Potter’s run into the area was picked out by Jaidon Anthony as his finish took a horrible deflection off Jarrad Branthwaite to beat Jordan Pickford.

Worse misfortune struck Everton two minutes later as Lewis-Potter’s shot was blocked by James Tarkowski, fell straight back into the path of the same Brentford player whose rebound was destined to be kept out again, only to hit Thierno Barry and wrong-foot Pickford.

The Toffees’ hopes of mounting a comeback were then all but ended five minutes before the interval when Tarkowski was penalised for a sliding tackle on Yehor Yarmoliuk.

Initially slow to award the free-kick, referee Craig Pawson eventually showed the Blues captain a yellow card – only to be called over by VAR and soon change his decision to red for violent conduct.

Left to battle on with 10 men, Everton had a sniff of a comeback with seconds left of the first half when fine work from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall ended with the No.8 chipping in a cross that Barry did well to nod into the bottom right-hand corner, only for keeper Caoimhin Kelleher to somehow claw the ball away.

Jack Grealish came on for the start of the second half and soon made an impact with a teasing centre across the six-yard box that just evaded Barry.

But any hopes of an unlikely fightback were ended on 67 minutes as Vitaly Janelt fired a 25-yard strike into the top right-hand corner.

And a miserable night was summed up in the dying moments when Damsgaard's corner found its way to substitute Fabio Carvalho to tap over the line from a yard out.

England head coach Thomas Tuchel described his relationship with Jude Bellingham as being “in a good place” after admitting it had been “a bit up and down”.

Tuchel has two Bellinghams in his latest England squad after calling up Jude’s brother, Jobe, for the first time for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. If they play together, it will be the first time brothers have represented England in the same team since Gary and Phil Neville 19 years ago.

This time last year, Tuchel cast doubt over Jude’s place in his team by picking Morgan Rogers over him, having not included the Real Madrid midfielder in an England squad the previous month.

But Jude performed superbly for Tuchel at the World Cup and was England’s best player during the last international camp. Tuchel revealed he has listened to his advice by calling up 21-year-old Jobe.

Asked if his relationship with Jude has developed, Tuchel said: “It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course, but we are in a good place.

Industry observers note that “I love to be his coach, he’s a top player, a very influential player and it goes both ways. If Jude was not feeling comfortable, he would not perform at that level.

It has been revealed that “At the moment, you see he’s happy to come into camp, he’s happy with the role he has, he’s fully invested and now to have the chance to have both of them [Bellingham brothers] is just the next step. I hope we have finished with the down. You never know as a coach.”.

Jobe has captained England’s Under-21s and, as well as U21 head coach Lee Carlsey, Tuchel acknowledged the influence of Jude on the Borussia Dortmund midfielder’s first senior call.

Jude once mentioned that playing with Jobe for England would be “the biggest dream of my life” and that it would mean more to him than any trophies.

Recent findings suggest that “This is also the signal that if you are good in the Under-21s, this is the next step. We had it with Elliot Anderson, we had it with Alex Scott, we have it with Jarell Quansah and it counts. If you play good for England in the Under-19s, 20s, 21s, if you play good for England in tournaments then it means something.”.

According to recent reports, tuchel at one point had to correct himself, with a laugh, when he accidentally referred to Jobe as Jube. It kicks off at the Stadio Georgios Karaisakis in Piraeus at 17.45 GMT (18.45 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game, Juventus-Omonia Nicosia and Borac-Atalanta on the Liveblog.

The Rossoneri might be doing well in Serie A, but their Europa League form has been appalling, losing three games without scoring a goal, making the 4-0 away to RB Salzburg an outlier.

Coach Ruben Amorim doesn’t even have the option of squad rotation today, because injuries ruled out Luka Modric, Francesco Camarda, Davide Bartesaghi, Strahinja Pavlovic, Samuel Chukwueze, Matteo Gabbia, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Pietro Terracciano.

With all that in mind, Goncalo Ramos is allowed no rest, supported by Diego Moreira and Cisse, but potentially moving Hutchinson into a central trequartista role.

Mike Maignan returns from suspension after his red card against Bournemouth.

Milan have never won away to a Greek side in Europe, managing just four draws and two defeats, including a 3-1 loss to Olympiacos in December 2018.

Olympiacos are still unbeaten in the Europa League so far this season, beating Jagiellonia, Olympique Marseille and Sparta Prague before the 0-0 at Stade Rennais.

Notably, they conceded only one goal in those four games and sit in sixth place.

They too have a few injury problems, because former Roma flop Leon Bailey, Chiquinho, Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, plus long-term absentees and cup-tied Yusuf Yazici, Balsa Popovic, Ayoub El Kaabi, Marius Mouandilmadji, Clayton, Joel Roca and Lorenzo Scipioni.

Former Inter defender Lorenzo Pirola is starting, with ex-Torino midfielder Marcus Pedersen and former Bologna midfielder Remo Freuler in the side.

Olympiacos: Ortega; Retsos, Smajlovic, Pirola, Bruno Onyemaechi; Freuler Gustavo Sá; Pedersen, Joao Silva, Gelson Martins; Gonzalez.

Milan: Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Jashari, Rabiot; Moreira, Cisse, Hutchinson; Ramos.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The female reporter Jude Bellingham defended during an 'intimidating' post-match interview has praised the England star for being 'respectful' and 'well-mannered' as she opened up on the viral incident.
  • BBC Sport reporter Elizabeth Conway was speaking to Bellingham after Real Madrid's 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday when another journalist interrupted her as she posed a follow-up question, threatening to cut her interview short.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 06:47 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 08:49 EST, 26 November 2026.

The female reporter Jude Bellingham defended during an 'intimidating' post-match interview has praised the England star for being 'respectful' and 'well-mannered' as she opened up on the viral incident.

BBC Sport reporter Elizabeth Conway was speaking to Bellingham after Real Madrid's 5-1 win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday when another journalist interrupted her as she posed a follow-up question, threatening to cut her interview short.

But the midfielder, 23, refused to answer the interferer and instead told him: 'Sorry, she's got one more [question].'.

Bellingham, who scored a sensational long-range goal on the hour mark to put Real Madrid ahead in the Champions League clash, was widely praised after footage of the incident went viral on social media, with fans applauding him as a 'class act' and 'role model for young men'.

Now Conway has added to the praise, stating the experience 'added a whole fresh layer to the love people have for Jude'.

Conway had been waiting to speak to the England star in the 'mixed zone' after the match – an area where journalists line up behind a barrier to interview players.

Jude Bellingham has won praise for his 'respectful' and 'classy' treatment of a female reporter.

BBC reporter Elizabeth Conway had been interrupted by a male reporter when asking her second question, leading to Bellingham's intervention. Source: instagram/@elizabeth.conway_.

'It is utter carnage,' she told BBC Radio WM, opening up on the incident at the Bernabeu. 'Obviously as an English reporter at Real Madrid, getting Jude is exactly what we want, it's gold dust.

It has been revealed that 'Jude very rarely gives interviews, especially in the mixed zone. It is chaos... It's kind of every person out for themselves.

'You've got elbows, you've got microphones, you've got cameras, you've got massive tall men reaching over you.

'I'm one of very, very few female reporters and one of very, very few English reporters there, so trying to make a stand for yourself and get in a good position is so key.'.

Conway admitted the mixed zone can be an 'intimidating' environment and being interrupted is unfortunately a routine part of being a post-match interviewer.

Admitting it was 'so nice' that Bellingham stepped in to stand up for her, she added: 'It's shown him yet again being respectful, polite, and really respecting me as a journalist.'.

Conway, originally from Solihull, specialises in Spanish football and is based in Madrid, according to her Instagram, where she has more than 12,000 followers.

She had asked Bellingham in the mixed zone what had gone through his mind when he scored with his sensational effort at the Bernabeu.

'Yeah, I was a bit surprised honestly,' Bellingham stated. 'I knew I could control the ball and get it into my grasp, but normally from there I am looking to see who's on as an option to play through.

In a recent development, 'It popped up nicely and I thought, you know, I am just going to hit it. It was a nice goal and important for the team being the second goal and gave us control.'.

The England superstar (right) had been in-demand after scoring with a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

After being interrupted and encouraged by Bellingham to pose her second question, Conway asked whether he feels like he is in the form of his life for club and country.

According to recent reports, 'My mentality is based more around just focusing on the next game, I think you are only as good as your next one. Your last one doesn't really matter,' Bellingham added.

'Even this one that has just gone past, it is all well and good and speaking to you guys is fun but my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game.'.

Conway later shared the exchange on social media, writing: 'Just Jude waiting for me to finish my questions,' adding a handshake emoji while fans were quick to praise Bellingham for his 'classy' moment.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked his goal, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'.

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported the 23-year-old is in advanced talks over a latest Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Bellingham has previously earned plaudits for his treatment of the media, having stopped to speak to a disabled reporter during the World Cup when several of his England team-mates had walked past, taking the time to answer his questions in Spanish.

The AfD and neo-Nazi networks: How close are the connections?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1187 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the electoral successes of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) have brought the party closer than ever to taking power in Germany.
  • This raises an even sharper question: what political ideas does the party stand for, which has been classified by Germany's domestic intelligence agency as a "suspected right-wing extremist" organization and, in several federal states, is already considered "confirmed right-wing extremist"?
  • Many political scientists have observed that the AfD has become increasingly radicalized since its founding in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the electoral successes of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) have brought the party closer than ever to taking power in Germany. For the 2029 federal election, it has set itself an ambitious goal: to see its co-chair Alice Weidel to become Germany's next chancellor.

This raises an even sharper question: what political ideas does the party stand for, which has been classified by Germany's domestic intelligence agency as a "suspected right-wing extremist" organization and, in several federal states, is already considered "confirmed right-wing extremist"?

Many political scientists have observed that the AfD has become increasingly radicalized since its founding in 2013.

"Viewed as a whole, the AfD is an extreme right-wing party that also displays tendencies associated with a fascist movement," said Fabian Virchow, a researcher on right-wing extremism at Düsseldorf University of Applied Sciences, in an interview with DW.

Industry observers note that virchow identifies different factions and strategic tendencies within the party, some of which are at odds with one another. Party leader Alice Weidel, for example, is generally seen as a proponent of a free-market approach that seeks to keep the state as small as possible. Others, by contrast, favor a strong state shaped by an ethnically homogeneous people, among them Björn Höcke, the influential far-right AfD leader in the state of Thuringia.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

It has been revealed that virchow sees a "normalization" of right-wing extremist positions within the AfD. In his view, this has made the party more attractive to neo-Nazi circles: "Today, many people see greater room for ethnonationalist and radical right-wing ideas.".

Sources indicate that support for this observation comes from the latest findings of the Leipzig Authoritarianism Study, one of the most widely cited long-term studies tracking right-wing extremist attitudes in Germany. The researchers behind the study have identified a rise in right-wing extremist views within German society, including a growing acceptance of ideologies rooted in the tradition of National Socialism.

Particularly striking is the finding that around two-thirds of people with firmly entrenched far-right worldviews would vote for the AfD. According to the study, the AfD has achieved what earlier far-right parties in Germany never managed: "to unite large segments of the electorate with anti-democratic attitudes behind it.".

According to recent reports, the debate has been further fueled by several recent incidents within the party. In 2026 alone, numerous AfD politicians and staff members made headlines over alleged ties to neo-Nazi organizations:.

According to recent reports, in August 2026, police carried out a large-scale raid targeting fifteen people. Authorities suspect them of continuing the activities of the so-called "Artgemeinschaft." Before it was banned in 2023, the group was considered one of Germany's largest and most influential neo-Nazi cadre organizations. Particularly explosive was the fact that two of those targeted in the raid are sitting AfD members of the Saxony-Anhalt state parliament. Their attorneys deny the allegations.

According to reporting by the German daily, Welt, four staff members of the AfD's parliamentary group in Saxony-Anhalt are former members of the now-banned "Heimattreue Deutsche Jugend" (HDJ), a neo-Nazi youth organization rooted in National Socialist racial ideology that organized paramilitary camps for young people. Two of the staff members held leadership positions within the HDJ and now work closely with AfD politician Ulrich Siegmund, who is seeking to become the AfD's first state premier in December.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that remarkably, both organizations, the "Artgemeinschaft" and the HDJ, are on the AfD's so-called incompatibility list, which is intended to draw a line between the party and extremist organizations and movements. In principle, anyone with a history of membership in such groups is supposed to be excluded from the party.

It has been revealed that but the list appears to be little more than a dead letter. In 2020, former AfD federal executive board member Andreas Kalbitz was expelled from the party after failing to disclose his membership in the "Heimattreue Deutsche Jugend" on his application to join. Yet according to the news magazine Spiegel, he is once again working for the AfD, this time as a staffer for Saxony-Anhalt state legislator Hans-Thomas Tillschneider, who has since become deputy speaker of the state parliament.

The question of the AfD's relationship to National Socialism has dogged the party since its founding in 2013. Even in its early years, co-founder and first party leader Bernd Lucke sparked controversy when he described democracy and parliamentary politics in Germany as "degenerate," a term the Nazis used to disparage art and culture that did not conform to their ideological worldview.

In Germany, references to the Nazi dictatorship (1933-1945) under Adolf Hitler remain politically taboo because of the country's responsibility for World War Two and the Holocaust, the systematic mass murder of Europe's Jews.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

If AfD members or their staff have come under scrutiny because of past involvement in ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations, they have generally sought to distance themselves from those backgrounds or from the ideologies associated with them.

According to recent reports, but how credible are these attempts at distancing? Laura Neumann* has worked with many people seeking to leave the far-right scene. She works for "Nordverbund Ausstieg Rechts," a network of organizations that supports far-right cadres and activists as they disengage from the movement. "A successful exit is the result of a professionally guided process," she said in an interview with DW.

It has been revealed that neumann describes leaving the far-right scene as a challenging process of self-confrontation. "When it comes to someone leaving the movement, the first question I always ask is: How does that person talk about their past? Have they genuinely come to terms with it?".

Based on the experience of exit counselors, one principle generally holds true: the longer and more deeply a person has been immersed in far-right circles, the more difficult it becomes to distance themselves from those beliefs and affiliations.

DW requested a statement from the AfD's federal executive board regarding its handling of party members who were previously active in ethnonationalist or neo-Nazi organizations. Individual lawmakers and parliamentary staff members were also asked to comment. None responded.

Sources indicate that the party's and its politicians' silence in the face of such allegations reflects an observation made by political scientist Fabian Virchow: "Within the AfD, there is no longer a perceived need to distance oneself from radical far-right positions. That is part of this process of normalization.".

Virchow states that right-wing extremism appears to have advanced so far into the mainstream of German society that efforts to scandalize it now remain largely ineffective.

It has been revealed that * Editor's note: To protect the privacy of the staff member of Nordverbund Ausstieg Rechts, we have changed her name to Laura Neumann. Her real name is known to the editors.

This article was originally written in German.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the copper-line page phone in Shaft #4 is going off, but it takes a minute for any of the miners to notice.
  • It has been revealed that it’s late morning, as measured by the water clocks and those who swear by them.
  • Industry observers note that this is one reason why the Mona Lisa Lottery, so loved by the old-timers, fails to stir up the same excitement it used to.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s a bell ringing in the Underground.

In a recent development, the copper-line page phone in Shaft #4 is going off, but it takes a minute for any of the miners to notice. They’re too busy dealing with a tunnel collapse and subsequent break in the geothermal line servicing Sectors 51–57.

It has been revealed that it’s late morning, as measured by the water clocks and those who swear by them. It’s midnight, as determined by the Moon and stars, cavorting a few thousand feet above their heads. But the oldest miner on this crew is 60, which is about 30 years too young to remember stars or moons, or appreciate the difference between morning and night.

Industry observers note that this is one reason why the Mona Lisa Lottery, so loved by the old-timers, fails to stir up the same excitement it used to. Too intent on repairs, the miners forget that the annual drawing is scheduled for today.

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

In a recent development, eventually, the ringing registers and curiosity calls them away from their work. Headlamps bob up and down in the dark. The sound of axes and drills drops off sharply, save for one stubborn miner still working, right below a rock face chiselled with the encouraging-but-long-false words: This Way Out.

Recent findings suggest that they gather round the ringer box and the foreman hushes them before pressing the phone tight to one ear, cupping his free hand over the other. Every noise echoes tenfold in the tunnels, and the foreman has to ask the voice on the other end to repeat themselves.

Industry observers note that “Abel?” the foreman repeats. “Are you sure?”.

A few miners huff wry laughs at the name, muttering, “Of course it’s him.”.

The foreman looks around, failing to find the lucky winner among his workers, “Well, where is he?”.

A couple outstretched thumbs and jerks of the head give the foreman his answer, unmistakably directed towards the only pickaxe still singing in the dark.

No one can opt out of the Mona Lisa Lottery. No one can give away their ticket to someone else.

But Abel’s tempted to decline the honour. He’s got work to do. And climbing up 2,000 feet to wait in line with the other winners for hours, all to stare at a square 30-by-21 inches for 5 whole minutes, doesn’t seem like a good use of his time.

It’s only Adèle, the old woman in the cave next door, who convinces him to make the trek upstairs.

Adèle was ten when the evacuations happened. She’s now two months shy of being a proper centenarian. Her mind isn’t as sharp as it used to be. She can’t remember what she had for breakfast, but she remembers the horrors they descended from well enough, all those lines of desperate people sent down below with canned goods, heirloom seeds and not much else.

Sources indicate that the treasures preserved from the Old World are few and Abel’s been given the chance to see one of the last. Arguably, the best. If she wasn’t blind as a bat, Adèle might kill him for his ticket. If she didn’t love him like a son, that is.

Industry observers note that “Don’t be a fool,” she tells him plainly. “Go see what you’ve been missing.”.

It has been revealed that the journey to the higher levels snakes up ladders and through tight squeezes, skirting the underbelly of the Safe Zone. There’s a breath of strange breeze up here, not conjured by any air machines. It makes some winners too nervous and they abandon the wait, rushing back down the way they came.

It has been revealed that abel’s not afraid. But he still thinks it’s a waste of time.

Sources indicate that adèle warned him that the wait for the Mona Lisa was just like this. When she was eight, her family waited for two hours just to get a glimpse. It doesn’t make sense to him. He doesn’t understand how a mere painting could be worth the trouble.

He’ll never know. Because that’s not what the Mona Lisa Lottery is all about. Despite the name, Abel’s not queuing for oil paint on a poplar panel.

The Mona Lisa is not in the Underground. They couldn’t waste the limited space. Leonardo’s lady still sits in the crumbling ruins of her museum gallery, her half-smile gone grimmer these days. She’s lonely without visitors. A wild boar passed her way a decade before, searching for truffles in the jungles of the overgrown Louvre. No one’s been by since.

She sighs into her patient smile; she waits with folded hands. Ever the optimist, she thinks her friends may return someday.

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game, Juventus-Omonia Nicosia and Borac-Atalanta on the Liveblog.

The Rossoneri absolutely must get points in Greece this evening, because they lost three of their four Europa League games so far this season, winning 4-0 away to RB Salzburg.

They make the trip without Luka Modric, Francesco Camarda, Davide Bartesaghi, Strahinja Pavlovic, Samuel Chukwueze, Matteo Gabbia, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Pietro Terracciano.

It is an all-attack formation, with Diego Moreira, Alphadjo Cisse, Omari Hutchinson and Goncalo Ramos together.

“In football, you need to defend and attack. Aside from the characteristics of the players, we need to attack with 11 and defend with 11,” Amorim told Sky Sport Italia.

Recent findings suggest that “The players know the positions that we want on the pitch, we are ready to play and must be more compact compared to the matches against Benfica and Ferencvaros. Even with these players, who are more attacking in their characteristics, we can defend better.”.

Milan have never won away to a Greek side in Europe, managing just four draws and two defeats, including a 3-1 loss to Olympiacos in December 2018.

It is notable that they have been unable to be consistent with two games in a week, so does Amorim see the right attitude today?

Sources indicate that “I think they understood, we watched the videos, we are improving as a team. We were a little soft against Ferencvaros because we were not compact, we need to really focus on the details, when the position makes all the difference two metres one way or another.

“We did it several times in Serie A, now we need to do it in the Europa League too.”.

Olympiacos can boast several former Serie A players, as Lorenzo Pirola was an Inter youth product, Remo Freuler spent time with Bologna and Atalanta, while Marcus Pedersen played for Torino.

“We need to be a good team, and to do that, we must be able to win in Serie A and in Europe. We have that responsibility, as we always say, the present is crucial, but we are in a long-term project. We need to know if we are ready and today is another important test for us to win,” concluded Amorim.

#141399. What has changed in James Bond films over the decades

What has changed in James Bond films over the decades

📅 05 Oct 2022 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1162 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios revealed on Monday that Robert Pattinson would be taking on the role of James Bond following Daniel Craig's departure after five hit films in the spy series.
  • This year alone, Pattinson has starred in "The Odyssey," "The Drama" and "Primetime." He is also famous for his role as "Twilight" vampire Edward Cullen.
  • The upcoming Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, an Oscar nominee known for movies such as the "Dune" trilogy and "Arrival.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios revealed on Monday that Robert Pattinson would be taking on the role of James Bond following Daniel Craig's departure after five hit films in the spy series.

This year alone, Pattinson has starred in "The Odyssey," "The Drama" and "Primetime." He is also famous for his role as "Twilight" vampire Edward Cullen.

The upcoming Bond movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, an Oscar nominee known for movies such as the "Dune" trilogy and "Arrival.".

According to recent reports, based on the spy novels by author Ian Fleming, the Bond franchise — about a British secret agent known for his charm and ⁠a ⁠fondness for martinis "shaken, not stirred" — is among the longest-running and highest-grossing in Hollywood history. ​​​​​​​.

Industry observers note that the first film in the series, "Dr. No," premiered in London on October 5, 1962.

Playing the leading role, Agent 007, was an unknown actor: Sean Connery.

In the film, we are first introduced to his character as he sits in a casino across from an attractive woman who is about to gamble away her fortune. When she asks 007 his name, the camera pans to Bond lighting a cigarette. With a smoldering look in his eye, he utters the legendary words: "Bond, James Bond.".

Shortly thereafter in the film, 007 receives an assignment to fly to Jamaica and investigate the murder of another M16 agent. He eventually tracks down a Chinese-German criminal scientist who is bent on destroying the US space program and achieving world domination.

Sources indicate that in principle, this story is the basis of all of 25 James Bond films. Whether the villain is Dr. No, Blofeld, Goldfinger or Le Chiffre, they all aim for one thing: world domination. But to do so, they have to get past James Bond whose gunfire and wild chase scenes inevitably spoil their plans.

Although many fan forums consider "Dr. No" to be one of the best Bond films, the movie would never be made in the same way today.

Firstly, one could write entire books about the omnipresent sexism and machismo that the character James Bond has displayed over the decades.

Certainly there would have to be a thick chapter dedicated to the women in his films, who are typically portrayed as naive, willingly flinging themselves into Bond's arms, seeking protection. Sometimes they are sophisticated female antagonists who lose control at the thought of hopping into bed with the secret agent.

In a recent development, whether friend of foe, each film had at least one Bond girl — and often more: More than 60 love interests have appeared in the films. Their names, like "Honey" or "Pussy Galore" would never be acceptable today. In more recent decades, female roles in Bond films have changed — as has Bond himself.

In the last five films in which Daniel Craig has played Bond, he is seen as a man who is tough on the outside and soft on the inside — and who is not always lucky with women.

Aside from the portrayal of women on screen, there are also plenty of other details in "Dr. No" that haven't quite stood the test of time.

Recent findings suggest that another sign of the zeitgeist in the 1962 film is that everyone smokes, which is a no-no by today's Hollywood standards. Cigarettes are found everywhere in the old film, from the casino to the hotel bar — and even the bedroom.

Smoking was commonplace in the US in the 1970s, so naturally this came across on the silver screen. In the 1970s TV series "Space: 1999" people were even depicted smoking on the moon, but by the 2000s, smoking was largely banned in many parts of the world due to its health risks.

One can also note in "Dr. No" that few people are wearing seat belts. When Bond drives off in his sports car to visit a woman, he is followed and a chase scene ensues. Bond, notably, is not wearing a seat belt.

His pursuers eventually drive off a slope and die, of course — after all, they aren't wearing seat belts either and cars didn't have airbags at the time. The vehicle explodes, prompting 007 to say, "They were obviously in a hurry to get to their own funeral.".

In the older Bond films, all secretaries and receptionists are played by women, which in the 1960s, were considered standard female jobs.

Whether redheaded, blonde or brunette, secretaries are Bond's favorite targets for womanizing and they are all susceptible to his charms.

Throughout most Bond films, the agent has a romantic tension with Moneypenny, his boss's secretary, something which was not described in the original books.

In the 2012 film "Skyfall" Moneypenny is given a first name: Eve, and we finally learn her backstory. In this film, she is no longer a hopeless secretary in love, but a top-trained agent who accidentally shoots Bond and is reassigned to desk duty as punishment.

In any case, today Moneypenny's job title today would probably be "Office Manager" or "Executive Assistant" rather than "Secretary.".

Industry observers note that in the film, Dr. No tells James Bond that he is the child of a British missionary and a Chinese woman from an upstanding family. However, the character is portrayed by Canadian actor Joseph Wiseman who is wearing makeup to make his eyes look more "Asian.".

While it used to be the norm in such movies to have East Asian characters played by white actors, today these cases of "yellowface" are frowned upon — just as it would be to wear blackface, putting black makeup on one's skin to portray a Black person.

Industry observers note that if there was a "Dr. No" remake in the future, a Chinese actor would be more likely to play this role.

Daniel Craig already paved the way in modernizing James Bond by stripping away campy gadgets, punchlines and invincibility, replacing them with a grounded, psychological and emotionally vulnerable portrayal of a post-9/11 spy.

Now it is up to Robert Pattinson to revisit the famous MI6 agent. Film critics believe his background will allow him to add dark sophistication and nonconformism to the iconic espionage role.

Throughout his career, Robert Pattinson has managed to combine roles in blockbuster hits and indie gems, from Bruce Wayne in "The Batman" to a disposable worker who is cloned every time he dies in "Mickey 17.".

It has been revealed that pattinson already has experience with classic spy archetypes: As the mysterious Neil in Christopher Nolan's sci-fi action thriller "Tenet," he assisted the protagonist in a time-bending espionage mission. He is also known for his eccentric personality and deadpan humor — qualities that could be useful for a modern Bond.

This article was translated from German by Sarah Hucal. It was first published in 2025 and updated following news of Robert Pattinson's casting as James Bond on November 16, 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hill Dickinson Stadium welcomed some of Liverpool’s care experienced young people for an exclusive behind-the-scenes tour to mark National Care Leavers Month. A group of 25 care leavers, who have either left or are preparing to leave local authority care, were given the opportunity to explore the Club’s stunning waterfront home. Observed every November, National Care Leavers Month is a UK-wide campaign that celebrates care experienced young people, amplifies their voices and promotes positive change in policy and practice. The youngsters, many of whom were visiting a football stadium for the first time, enjoyed an informative tour of the state-of-the-art venue, including the impressive home dressing room, the Media Centre, pitchside areas and learning about the heritage of the historic site. Jenny Glennard, Corporate Director of Children & Young People’s Services at Liverpool City Council, said: "On behalf of Liverpool Children's Social Care, I would like to again extend my gratitude to Everton for providing our care experienced young people with the fantastic opportunity to visit Hill Dickinson Stadium as part of National Care Leavers Month. "To be given a personal group tour was an experience and memory they will never forget. All of our young people have expressed how much they enjoyed the day and how impressed they were with the stadium, as well as the staff who made them feel so welcome. "We value our relationship with Everton and look forward to continuing to work with the Club in the future." Liverpool City Council's Leaving Care Services provide a wide range of support for young people transitioning from local authority care. Using a person-centred approach to independent living skills, planning and assessment, the service aims to improve outcomes across education, training, employment, health and accommodation. For more information on Liverpool City Council's Leaving Care Services, click here.

NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (641 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Well, imagine having to travel 3,300 years to get to your destination.
  • Imagine departing in 1977 and arriving in 2026, on November 18 at 11:16 a.m.
  • NASA's Voyager 1, a spacecraft launched almost half-a-century ago, has traveled a light-day from Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hate long-haul flights? Well, imagine having to travel 3,300 years to get to your destination.

Imagine departing in 1977 and arriving in 2026, on November 18 at 11:16 a.m. Central European Time to be precise, and then, not stopping but continuing the journey.

NASA's Voyager 1, a spacecraft launched almost half-a-century ago, has traveled a light-day from Earth.

Recent findings suggest that A light-day is the distance light covers in 24 hours — about 26 billion kilometers (or around 16 billion miles). Put another way: Light does in one day what it took the spacecraft 49 years, two months and 11 days to do.

But Voyager 1 is not only far away, it is also traveling at an incredible speed of 61,000 km/h (38,000 mph).

When Voyager 1 released, it was in sync with a planetary alignment that was as rare as the spacecraft itself — one that happens only once every 176 years. It was the alignment Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, which scientists wanted to investigate.

Once the original mission was accomplished, Voyager 1 used the planets Jupiter and Saturn to perform a gravitational slingshot.

According to recent reports, it flew close to each planet, got pulled and accelerated by their massive gravity, and swung around faster than before. And that is how Voyager 1 has achieved its speed.

In the vacuum of space, nothing slows you down.

On Valentine's Day 1990, from beyond Neptune, Voyager 1 took the only portrait of the solar system from the outside ever made by a spacecraft.

In 2012, it became the first human-made object to reach interstellar space.

Its journey is ongoing. In about 40,000 years — long after its plutonium power supply dies out — it will still be flying and pass by the star Gliese 445, which is more than 17 light-years away from Earth.

That's light-years, not light-days. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year. It will take Voyager 1 about 18,000 years to reach the one light-year milestone.

Voyager 1 is destined to wander the Milky Way "perhaps eternally," as NASA puts it.

The spacecraft is the first human-made object ever to be one light-day away from home.

"If you want to say 'hello' to Voyager, you send your message and then you go home and you wait two days before you finally get a response," notes Suzanne Dodd, the mission's project manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

Industry observers note that but you do get a response. Even today it sends back data that helps scientists on Earth.

"[It's] still working great, sending back data from a region of space no other human-made craft has ever explored," indicates Kareem Badaruddin, the mission manager at JPL.

No story about Voyager 1 seems complete without mentioning The Golden Record, a phonographic record, that is part of the spacecraft's cargo.

It has been revealed that the spacecraft is carrying other Earthly objects as messages and artefacts from Earth for extraterrestrials. But the Golden Record is what we tend to focus on because it contains soundbites representing languages and cultures from around our planet.

We're told it's very unlikely that any intelligent lifeform will ever receive the cargo or even know how to play The Golden Record.

But if they do get the record and work out how to play it, the first thing they will hear is a controversial voice — not one of Earthly unity, as was the original idea. Those are the words of Kurt Waldheim, a former UN Secretary-General (1972-81) and Austrian President (1986-92), whose concealed wartime past as a German army officer in the Balkans surfaced a decade after Voyager 1's launch. It was alleged Waldheim had participated in Nazi crimes.

"He’s developing nicely. He’s got plenty of work still to do but with all the guys their appetite to work and seek improvement and develop has been outstanding. "We tell them that if you want a career in the game then winning is essential and you need the mentality to keep improving your performance. Within that as individuals you have to show grit and steel and play with character and personality.".

Kamara tested Barnsley from a narrow angle on 62 minutes and from the subsequent corner kick Ryan Watson headed over, and at the other end Melvin Matos was desperately unfortunate to see his superbly struck shot strike the Rovers crossbar.

To their credit, Everton stuck at it and kept themselves in the game. Olayiwola was next to try his luck but from distance he thumped the ball high over the bar.

Boyce-Clarke had to be alert again in added time to keep out a snapshot volley from Matos.

Harvey Foster was excellent in the first half, Will Tamen was outstanding and there were some really good performances so we’re really pleased.

"Melvin Matos is relentless. He’s got this unbelievable knack of pressing the life out of people and closing the space very promptly. If he can get his first touch out of his feet and run at the backline, he’s a threat.

"He’s developing nicely. He’s got plenty of work still to do but with all the guys their appetite to work and seek improvement and develop has been outstanding.

The good news is Juve have Francisco Conceicao back in the starting XI for his first appearance since the shoulder injury on October 18.

He is part of a 3-4-2-1 formation with Ekhator as centre-forward and Boga in the trident.

Neto also gets his first start in goal for Juventus, albeit in his second spell at the club, having last featured in this jersey in May 2017.

Omonia Nicosia sit fourth in their domestic league, and had originally been in the Champions League preliminary rounds, dropping into the Europa League.

They started this season strong, beating Celta Vigo and Celje, but then lost 4-1 at home to Benfica and 3-1 away to NEC Nijmegen.

They have Fotis Kitsos and Mihlali Mayambela injured, while Carel Eiting, Moses Odubajo, David Akintola and Giorgos Viktoros are cup-tied.

Lois Diony is by a long way their top scorer this season with 11 goals in 20 competitive appearances, but only one in the Europa League.

Juventus: Neto; Gatti, Lucumi, Kelly; Cabal, Douglas Luiz, Sarr, Cambiaso; Conceicao, Boga; Ekhator.

Omonia Nicosia: Kaminski; Duverne, Coulibaly, Satka, Nego; Andreou, Maric; Tanase, Tankovic, Montnor; Kakoullis.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

French Football Federation (FFF) President Philippe Diallo has received UEFA backing to be a candidate in FIFA's presidential election, which will take place in March in Morocco, with criticism against current chief Gianni Infantino growing.

UEFA, European football's governing body, stated it has backed Diallo "unanimously" in a bid to replace Infantino, putting it's "full support" behind the Frenchman.

Veteran Japanese official Kohzo Tashima has also confirmed his candidacy, with the deadline for candidates to stand for election being November 18.

Potential candidates for the post must show letters of support from five of FIFA's 211 member associations before going through eligibility and integrity checks.

Diallo, the 63-year-old head of the FFF, is the son of a Senegalese boxing champion.

He was elected as the federation's president in 2023 with a large majority. He was reelected for another four-year term in 2024.

Back in September, Diallo remarked the FFF had withdrawn its support for Infantino ahead of the March 2027 election, saying trust in the FIFA president had "been betrayed.".

"The way in which the governance of world football is envisaged no longer reflects us," the French football head remarked of the decision.

If elected, the Frenchman would become FIFA's first black president, as well as it's third French leader after Robert Guerin and Jules Rimet, who served as the organization's first and third presidents.

Gianni Infantino has been in charge of world football's governing body since 2016.

He has been facing growing criticism since pitching a blueprint of sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors. The criticism of the plan was led by UEFA and its President Aleksander Ceferin.

Infantino ended up scrapping the proposal but UEFA went ahead and took FIFA to court in the US, trying to gather evidence ahead of potentially lodging a criminal complaint with Swiss authorities about alleged "mismanagement" by Infantino.

FIFA's headquarters are located in Zürich, Switzerland.

Infantino was also criticized after creating a peace prize and awarding it to US President Donald Trump last year.

The connection between Infantino and Trump came under criticism once again during the World Cup, after United States forward Folarin Balogun was allowed to take part in the round-of-16 game against Belgium despite having been shown a red card in the previous game.

The US president admitted to having personally intervened through a conversation with Infantino.

A pregnant person with dengue speaks to a nurse in Peru, which has been hit by a surge of cases this year. Credit: Juan Carlos Cisneros/AFP/Getty.

The debilitating viral disease called dengue has exploded in incidence far more than previously thought, a latest analysis suggests.

The number of reported global cases of dengue, which is transmitted by infected mosquitoes, rose from 430,000 in 1990 to 14.7 million in 2024 — a 34-fold increase, the analysis indicates.

Dengue is spreading in Europe: how worried should we be?

Dengue is spreading in Europe: how worried should we be?

The data were presented on 22 November at the annual meeting of the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene (ASTMH) in National Harbor, Maryland. Scientists also provided some of the strongest results yet about a counter-intuitive way to curb the disease’s staggering spread: the release of specially modified mosquitoes. But researchers also presented discouraging data on other solutions, and scientists at the meeting emphasized that the campaign to beat back dengue will be complicated and costly.

It has been revealed that “We’re in an extraordinary and pivotal moment” in the history of studying mosquito-borne illnesses, said Albert Ko, president of ASTMH. Trial results presented at the meeting demonstrated, he said, that “we can get rigorous evidence on what works, what doesn’t and what needs to be done to scale these effective interventions to protect the 4 billion people” around the world who are exposed to dengue and other mosquito-borne illnesses.

Industry observers note that dengue causes fever, headaches and severe bone pain. It is transmitted mainly by Aedes aegypti, a species of mosquito that thrives in warm, urban environments. Global warming and increased urbanization have expanded the mosquitoes’ range. Existing vaccines provide imperfect protection.

According to recent reports, cases of dengue are often recorded in disparate databases that aren’t easily comparable, says Ahyoung Lim, an infectious-disease modeler at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, who was involved in the study on dengue incidence. The results have also been published as a preprint1 on Research Square ahead of peer review. This has meant that no single database has captured the total number of reported dengue cases over time, leading Lim and her team to compile the most complete record of reported cases and use statistical modelling tools to fill in gaps in which data were missing.

Recent findings suggest that the staggering increase in reported cases isn’t surprising, says Eng Eong Ooi, a dengue virologist at Duke–NUS Medical School in Singapore, who was not involved in the research. Populations in urban environments around the world are steadily increasing, he says, which means that “more and more people are living at risk of dengue each year”.

One promising approach to curb dengue starts with breeding mosquitoes and deliberately infecting them with a bacterium called Wolbachia that reduces the insects’ ability to transmit viruses. When released into the wild, these infected mosquitoes pass the bacterium on to their offspring, eventually lowering the number of highly transmissive mosquitoes.

This is the world’s largest ‘mosquito factory’: its goal is to stop dengue.

This is the world’s largest ‘mosquito factory’: its goal is to stop dengue.

Recent findings suggest that at the ASTMH meeting, another team of researchers shared results from the first randomized controlled trial in the Americas to test Wolbachia’s effect on dengue transmission. Between January 2021 and May 2022, the researchers released roughly 32 million Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes across designated regions of Brazil and monitored almost 6,000 children living inside and outside these regions. The children provided annual blood samples between 2020 and 2024, and the reseachers found that those in the Wolbachia regions were 68% less likely to be infected with dengue compared with those in non-Wolbachia regions.

These positive results mark an important milestone in proving Wolbachia’s potential to drastically reduce dengue cases, claims Elisabeth Nelson, an epidemiologist at the Yale School of Public Health in New Haven, Connecticut, and a researcher on the trial.

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 08:48 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 10:35 EST, 26 November 2026.

A referee was replaced at half-time of an Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League Two match after he was accused of 'being drunk' by a manager of one of the teams – a claim the official has denied.

Syrian referee Hanna Hattab oversaw the match between United Arab Emirates' side Al Jazira and Iran's Gol Gohar in Asia's second tier club competition.

Controversy emerged in the 32nd minute after Hattab awarded a free-kick after a foul by Al Jazira's Felício Milson.

Hattab initially waved away protests from Al-Jazira players and approached Milson holding a yellow card.

The official then stunned players after appearing to receive a message in his earpiece, before turning and walking towards Al-Jazira goalkeeper Ersin Destanoglu.

Hattab revealed the goalkeeper a yellow card, despite him being nearly half the pitch away from the incident.

Referee Hanna Hattab was accused by a manager of 'being drunk' following a controversial decision in an Asian Champions League Two match - a claim the official has denied.

The referee was then seen speaking to his fourth official, leading to him rescinding the goalkeeper's yellow card while Milson escaped being shown a second yellow card for his challenge.

Al Jazira scored the only goal of the game minutes later through Anderson Talisca, but the bizarre incident involving Hattab was reportedly the centre of discussion at half-time.

Gol Gohar head coach Mehdi Rahmati had reportedly been seen shouting 'he's drunk' at the official, while the club's sporting director claimed post-match they would have refused to play the second half had Hattab remained in charge.

'The referee against Al Jazira was not in a normal state, and even Al Jazira's players told us the same thing,' said Heydar Afsari.

'The club immediately informed the match officials and warned them that we would not play if the situation remained the same.'.

Hattab was ultimately replaced by the fourth official for the second half of the match.

The referee, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing pool, has since released a statement hitting back at the allegation.

'I will wait for the official communication and official stance from the Syrian Arab Football Federation, and I will also communicate with the people and parties responsible for me locally and internationally, before issuing an official statement that clarifies all the details and facts related to what happened,' Hattab wrote.

The claim had centred on the referee appearing to listen to his earpiece and changing his mind on booking an Al Jazira player, before bizarrely showing a yellow card to their goalkeeper.

Al Jazira's goalkeeper appeared stunned by his yellow card, which was later rescinded with the referee then being replaced at half-time of the match.

'In conclusion, I confirm that family and personal life are not the responsibility of others, and are not a game in your hands.

'Religion, reason, and morals do not tolerate the insult of people's privacy or defamation of them.

'I also confirm my full right to take all legal and judicial measures against anyone who published or made a statement or contributed to the insult and defamation of me, regardless of their position or status, whether they are an individual, an institution, or a sports entity.'.

Omani sports journalist Issa Remarked, who covers Asian competitions, also came to Hattab's defence and insisted the claim the official was drunk is false.

'What happened to him was due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus,' he wrote on social media,.

'He underwent a medical examination after the match and was not intoxicated, contrary to what has been circulating.'.

The Syrian Football Federation added in a statement: 'Following an assessment of his health, it has been confirmed - contrary to various claims circulating on social media- that the reports regarding his situation are entirely unfounded.

'The Committee reiterates its unwavering support for him and is committed to thoroughly investigating all details and circumstances surrounding the incident.

'In this regard, the Committee has contacted the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) to request the referee’s medical report, the match commissioner’s report, and the referee assessor’s report, in order to accurately ascertain the facts of the incident and take the necessary follow-up actions.'.
