📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Omari Hutchinson kept Milan’s Europa League hopes alive by inspiring the 4-2 comeback win away to Olympiacos with a goal and two assists for Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic, then Diego Moreira late on.

It has been revealed that the Rossoneri had a terrible record in the Europa League, losing three of their four matches without finding the net, with a 4-0 victory away to RB Salzburg the outlier. They made the trip to Greece without Luka Modric, Francesco Camarda, Davide Bartesaghi, Strahinja Pavlovic, Samuel Chukwueze, Matteo Gabbia, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Pietro Terracciano, so squad rotation was kept to a minimum.

Olympiacos were still unbeaten with three wins and a draw, but missed Leon Bailey, Chiquinho, Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, plus long-term absentees and cup-tied Yusuf Yazici, Balsa Popovic, Ayoub El Kaabi, Marius Mouandilmadji, Clayton, Joel Roca and Lorenzo Scipioni.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

Diego Moreira was valuable in defence during the opening minutes when charging down the Martins effort after a Panagiotis Retsos cross from the right.

Gelson Martins had a couple of pops from distance, but the first real chance was on 22 minutes with a curler that Maignan flew to palm around the upright.

It has been revealed that olympiacos were increasing the pressure and broke the deadlock with former Inter defender and Italy Under-21 international Pirola’s header, in off the underside of the crossbar from a Gustavo Sa corner. UEFA credited it as a Maignan own goal because the ball hadn’t completely crossed the line until it hit the goalkeeper on the way off the bar.

Pirola was every bit as decisive four minutes later, because Alphadjo Cisse had sprinted away on the counter, was tackled by the on-rushing goalkeeper, but still managed to prod it towards the empty net, only for the Italian defender to rush back for a desperate goal-line clearance.

It should’ve been 2-0 in added time, as Bruno Onyemaechi pulled back from the left for Pirola to fire over undisturbed from 10 yards.

It has been revealed that milan introduced Christian Pulisic and Yunus Musah for the restart, but instead went 2-0 down. Maignan made the save on the Joao Silva angled drive, but as the move continued, the same player ran onto the Freuler through ball to blast into the roof of the net from just inside the area.

It has been revealed that just as Olympiacos were pouring forward for a third, they were caught by a rapid counter-attack. Hutchinson started the move from inside his own half, rode two tackles and cut inside to drill low into the far bottom corner to give Milan some hope.

Hutchinson contributed to the equaliser too as the comeback was completed, his cross from the right finding Cisse to squirm away from his marker to nod in at the back post.

It has been revealed that hutchinson was simply unstoppable in the second half when used out wide on the right, and he provided his second assist to turn the game around, met by the fantastic Pulisic volley from 12 yards with the right boot. It was the American’s fifth goal in his last six appearances.

Incredible work from Omari Hutchinson, who sets up Christian Pulisic for a fine volley 👌.

📺 Stream live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/eNxR1252Q6.

— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 26, 2026.

Cisse’s acrobatic bicycle kick didn’t quite come off from yet another Hutchinson cross, while Pirola’s risky interception prevented Adrien Rabiot meeting the Moreira assist.

In the final minute, penalty appeals were rejected because a header was charged down by Fikayo Tomori’s shoulder, but then Milan wasted the chance to add a fourth on the counter with Pulisic ballooning over.

With the last kick of the game, Hutchinson broke away on the counter from an Olympiacos corner, sent Pulisic down the left, he rolled across for Moreira to take a touch, then sweep in from 12 yards for 4-2.

The Rossoneri had never been able to beat a Greek team away from home before, managing only four draws and two defeats, including a 3-1 loss to Olympiacos in December 2018.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia on Tuesday said it had created a board-level national security and export-control committee.

This follows the scandal surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week over extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China and working to help ensure higher quality chips crucial to AI development made it to the Chinese market.

The events have heightened oversight of the US tech giant and its importance to national security, as well as wiping several hundred billion dollars off the stock market valuation of what investors treat as the world's most valuable company in the space of a month.

Recent findings suggest that since Huang's resignation, some investors — including Elon Musk and Donald Trump — have voiced concern that his departure could leave Nvidia and America's AI sector in peril and are now calling for his return. Huang on Tuesday, expressed regret for "serious mistakes" in his personal life before declaring he would be "honored" to return if the company's board of directors thought that was "in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America.".

Nvidia is calling the fresh group its National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee.

Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former vice chair at Goldman Sachs, will chair the committee, joined by fellow directors Stephen Neal, a former CEO of a law firm, John Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical engineering at the California Institute of Technology (Caltech).

The committee will meet at least once every quarter. It will also incorporate independent legal, national security and trade compliance experts.

Nvidia already has a lower-level National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team; these groups will report to the board-level committee.

"We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation," Board Chair Harvey Jones said in a statement.

The company did not explicitly link the decision to November's developments and Huang's rapid fall from grace, but the timing seemed conspicuous.

The decision was announced hours ahead of Nvidia publishing its third-quarter results, with its still-stratospheric share price having fallen roughly 28% in the past month.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US President Donald Trump, whom Huang was influential in persuading to allow the export of better-quality Nvidia chips to China than other US companies and officials deemed prudent, welcomed Nvidia's move on arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday.

"Yes, that's a good idea. It's a great company," he remarked during a photo opportunity at a Manila meeting with the other "Quad" leaders from Australia, India and Japan. "It's a great idea.".

According to recent reports, trump reportedly owned Nvidia stock worth tens of millions of dollars before the share price fell. He also owns shares in other massive tech companies.

Recent findings suggest that huang resigned last week after admitting to extramarital affairs in a message to Nvidia employees. This followed widespread reports, seemingly based on US and other intelligence, that one of the affairs was with a woman who used to lead a Singapore-based cloud computing firm.

That firm, Megaspseed International, is a major Nvidia client and is suspected of diverting advanced chips to China in violation of US export controls. Intelligence officials also suspect Huang's partner of being an asset of Chinese intelligence services.

The reporting on the case also seems to show these suspicions had been known to US officials and other countries, including Singapore, for roughly a year.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea are considering a surprise move to bring Antonio Rüdiger back to Stamford Bridge in January as Xabi Alonso looks to address his side’s defensive problems.
  • The 33-year-old Real Madrid defender is approaching the final months of his contract, potentially making him available for a significantly reduced transfer fee during the winter window.
  • Chelsea’s recent struggles have highlighted the need for greater experience and leadership at the back, and a reunion with Rüdiger could offer a relatively inexpensive solution.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea are considering a surprise move to bring Antonio Rüdiger back to Stamford Bridge in January as Xabi Alonso looks to address his side’s defensive problems.

The 33-year-old Real Madrid defender is approaching the final months of his contract, potentially making him available for a significantly reduced transfer fee during the winter window.

Chelsea’s recent struggles have highlighted the need for greater experience and leadership at the back, and a reunion with Rüdiger could offer a relatively inexpensive solution.

According to former Premier League scout Bryan King, speaking to Football Insider, Chelsea are considering bringing Rüdiger back to west London.

The German international has struggled for regular opportunities under José Mourinho at Real Madrid, failing to feature in any of their last five La Liga matches.

Rüdiger previously worked under Alonso at Madrid and recently spoke positively about the Spaniard’s managerial qualities and Chelsea’s project.

However, the Blues could face competition from another Premier League club.

Manchester United are also monitoring Rüdiger, with Mauricio Pochettino’s side considering either a January move or a free transfer next summer.

Chelsea’s existing relationship with the defender and his familiarity with Alonso could potentially give them an advantage.

Chelsea’s recruitment strategy has largely focused on signing younger players with considerable long-term potential, but their current defensive problems suggest a more balanced approach is required.

Rüdiger would bring aggression, leadership, physicality and extensive experience of competing at the highest level.

Having helped Chelsea win the Champions League in 2021, he also understands the expectations that come with representing the club.

His presence could benefit younger defenders such as Levi Colwill and Josh Acheampong, while providing Alonso with a trusted option during a challenging period.

There are understandable concerns regarding his age, recent injury history and wage demands. Chelsea should therefore avoid offering an excessively lucrative long-term contract.

However, if Real Madrid are willing to negotiate an affordable January transfer, bringing Rüdiger back could represent an excellent piece of short-term business.

Chelsea do not necessarily need another expensive defensive prospect. They need someone capable of organising their backline, taking responsibility and making an immediate impact.

Rüdiger could be exactly that player.

Arsenal face competition from Chelsea and Tottenham for highly-rated 21-year-old.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea star Cole Palmer has been the subject of criticism from ex-Blue Pat Nevin, who has admitted it’s getting harder to keep making excuses for him.

Palmer’s noticeable dip in form has been well-documented, with the England international not contributing nearly as much as he did in his first two seasons at Stamford Bridge.

Nevin has reluctantly admitted he’s concerned about Palmer, as enough time has passed now that the former Manchester City man can’t keep relying on excuses like coming back from an injury or playing in an unfamiliar role.

Speaking to Simon Phillips, Nevin expressed his concern about Palmer and attempted to explain what might have gone wrong for the 24-year-old.

“There is a concern over Cole Palmer, I have to admit, though I hate admitting it. He was injured for large periods of last season, so he’s been going through injury recovery. You give him a slight pass for that.

“Then he was playing slightly out of position because Enzo Fernandez was in a central position, so you think that’s probably why he was peripheral.

“But, can we stop this now? Can we actually say: ‘Cole, you’ve got to do it mate, it’s time now. It’s time to get back to that player that you were, controlling situations and doing genius things again.’.

In a recent development, want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

“It feels as if I’m always making excuses for Cole at the moment, but in the end, the numbers start telling you. Is he overthinking it? Because when Cole is at his very best, you can tell it’s completely off the cuff.

In a recent development, “There’s something about young players when they come through, it’s a bit easier because you act on instinct. Sometimes that instinct goes because you overthink or because you’re over-coached.

Industry observers note that “There are technical demands put on you like: ‘You must go to that part of the pitch.’ Well, wait a minute, maybe that’s not where I feel most dangerous in this game. I’d love to get inside the head of Cole Palmer, but it doesn’t look like an easy place to get inside, if I’m honest.

“Has he got the quality and skills to come back and be that player again? Yeah, of course he has. It’s a bit like Phil Foden, player of the year, amazing stuff, and then he had a complete period where he couldn’t score or create a great deal.

It has been revealed that “It was hard to understand how that was even possible, but you can get it back. Phil’s doing well again now, and Cole can do it as well.

It has been revealed that “The one thing I would underline is that it has nothing to do with being left out of the England squad. That’s absolutely not the case. Looking at Cole Palmer, there is no way he can blame England, Thomas Tuchel, or anything like that. Absolutely not.”.

It’s hard to know precisely what Palmer needs right now, but it’s been a generally chaotic period at Chelsea and that probably hasn’t helped him.

Palmer’s best form came under Mauricio Pochettino in his first season in west London, and since then he’s played under three different managers, not including caretaker or interim managers.

This is far from ideal for Palmer and many would argue he’s not the only one in this CFC squad struggling to perform at their best.

New manager Xabi Alonso has not quite had the desired impact yet and that’s been an matter for a few players in this squad, such as Estevao Willian and pretty much the entire defence.

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (397 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) ruled against Turkey over the detention of human rights lawyer and elected lawmaker Can Atalay.
  • The ECHR published its decision on Tuesday, saying that Turkey must release Atalay and allow him to take up his seat in the Turkish parliament.
  • The court ruled that his continued detention had been intended to silence him and undermine political pluralism.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) ruled against Turkey over the detention of human rights lawyer and elected lawmaker Can Atalay.

The ECHR published its decision on Tuesday, saying that Turkey must release Atalay and allow him to take up his seat in the Turkish parliament.

The court ruled that his continued detention had been intended to silence him and undermine political pluralism.

It ordered Turkey to pay him €32,500 (about $35,700) in compensation.

The judges stressed that Atalay's case should not be considered separately, but rather in the wider context of the detention of political opponents, human rights activists and journalists in Turkey.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Turkey was among the original signatories of the European Convention on Human Rights. Yet it has previously refused to comply with the court's decisions in the cases of rights activist Osman Kavala and prominent Kurdish politician Selahattin Demirtas.

As a lawyer, Atalay represented victims in numerous social and political cases in Turkey, as well as in freedom of speech cases involving journalists and writers.

He was also among the leading voices in the 2013 Gezi protests, which the government called an attempted coup.

Because of his involvement in the protests, Atalay, along with seven others, was sentenced to 18 years in prison in April 2022 for "aiding and abetting an attempted coup.".

Continuing his struggle from the infamous Silivri prison, Atalay ran as a candidate for the Workers' Party of Turkey (TIP) in the 2023 parliamentary elections.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A candidate for the earthquake-hit province of Hatay, he won his seat but was denied release despite multiple rulings by the Constitutional Court, Turkey's top court.

His parliamentary status was revoked in 2024, a decision the Constitutional Court later overturned. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's party stopped the opposition from formally reading the decision in parliament.

Although a year later an opposition lawmaker read the decision in parliament, Atalay remains in jail.

After the ECHR's ruling was published, TIP leader Erkan Bas took to social media to call for Atalay's release and the restoration of his parliamentary mandate.

There was also still time for a red card for Youri Tielemans on a crazy night, as the Argentine head coach picked up his first point as United boss.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During talks on ending the war in Ukraine, Russian representatives in Abu Dhabi presented a document containing far-reaching demands, The Latest York Times reports.

Dated November 10, the document reportedly calls not only for an end to Western arms deliveries to Ukraine but also for NATO to withdraw its troops and bases and move them back to where they were in 1997.

Recent findings suggest that the year 1997 refers to the NATO alliance before its first eastward expansion, according to the Kremlin. At the time, NATO had 16 members. Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary had already been invited to join but did not formally become members of the defense alliance until two years later. In the following years, more countries in Central, Eastern and Southeastern Europe joined, followed most recently by countries in Scandinavia. Today, NATO has 32 member states in Europe and North America.

According to the report, Russia is not explicitly demanding that Central and Eastern European countries leave, but rather that the NATO alliance end its military presence in those countries.

Sources indicate that A withdrawal of NATO troops and bases from member states that joined the alliance after 1997 would significantly weaken their defense capabilities. For example, since 2004, NATO allies, including Germany, have taken turns policing the airspace over Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.

Recent findings suggest that because the Baltic states do not have fighter jets of their own for independent air policing, NATO provides the capability. Since 2026, the mission has been part of a broader air defense presence. The planned deployment of the German Lithuania Brigade, which is expected to be fully operational by the end of 2027, would also have to be halted.

In Romania, meanwhile, the Mihail Kogalniceanu Air Base near Constanța on the Black Sea is currently being expanded. Once completed, it is set to become Europe's largest NATO air base by area — even larger than Ramstein in Germany.

"Under no circumstances will we allow anyone to establish upcoming security rules for this part of the world over the heads of Poland and Europe," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk told TVP World. His Bulgarian counterpart, Rumen Radev, called a NATO withdrawal "unthinkable and unrealistic." No country should be forced by external pressure to reverse its decision on which alliance to join.

Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal also rejected any Russian say in changes to Europe's security order: "We have nothing to discuss with Russia about Europe's security order; it is working well.".

The strong rejection from the capitals of NATO's eastern members, however, masks fears along the alliance's eastern flank that a deal between Washington and Moscow could turn their security into a bargaining chip.

According to recent reports, in the event of an armed attack on a NATO member, the other alliance members are obligated under Article 5 to come to its aid. Each member decides for itself what measures it considers necessary, which may include the use of military force.

For the mutual defense commitment to deter a potential aggressor, that country must believe NATO can intervene militarily promptly and effectively in a crisis. The deployment of allied troops along the eastern flank serves precisely this purpose. A withdrawal would make defense more difficult and could lead Russia to believe that an attack on NATO territory would involve fewer risks for Moscow.

Sources indicate that as part of their security framework, European countries have agreed that states are free to decide which alliances they wish to join. NATO points to Article 10 of its founding treaty, which enshrines its open-door policy for European countries. The 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act also explicitly stated that neither side had the right to veto the other's decisions.

Back in November 1990, the participating states of the Conference on Security and Cooperation in Europe (CSCE), including the Soviet Union, had already agreed in the Charter of Paris to respect each country's freedom to choose its own security arrangements.

During the negotiations surrounding German reunification, then-US Secretary of State James Baker and German Foreign Minister Hans-Dietrich Genscher used language that suggested putting limits on NATO's eastward expansion.

Their remarks came during discussions about unified Germany's membership in NATO and the possible deployment of NATO forces on the territory of the former East Germany. However, no written, legally binding general promise was ever agreed that NATO would never expand to include other former Warsaw Pact countries.

Recent findings suggest that in the 1997 NATO-Russia Founding Act, both sides declared that they no longer considered each other adversaries. NATO stated that, under the security conditions prevailing at the time and in the foreseeable future, it intended to ensure its collective defense through reinforcement rather than the additional permanent stationing of "substantial combat forces." The agreement explicitly gave Moscow no veto over NATO decisions.

Recent findings suggest that in the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, Russia, the United States and the United Kingdom reaffirmed their commitment to respect Ukraine's independence and existing borders and to refrain from the use of force. These assurances were linked to Ukraine's decision to give up its nuclear weapons. However, the memorandum did not oblige the United States or the United Kingdom to defend Ukraine militarily in the event of an attack. NATO membership was not addressed at the time.

Just over two months before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the Kremlin presented two draft treaties to the United States and NATO. In them, Russia demanded an end to further NATO enlargement. The draft agreement with NATO also proposed that Russia and NATO members that had already joined the alliance as of May 27, 1997, refrain from deploying additional troops or weapons on the territory of other European countries beyond the levels stationed there on that date.

Security guarantees for the postwar period and a future security framework for Europe were also on the agenda in Abu Dhabi. Negotiating NATO troop deployments and alliance enlargement alongside an end to the war in Ukraine would give Moscow additional leverage. Russia has long maintained that the "root causes" of the war must be addressed. The Kremlin includes NATO enlargement and the alliance's military presence in Eastern Europe among those causes.

Sources indicate that so far, no significant Western player has expressed willingness to accept Russia's demands in Abu Dhabi. On the contrary, former Polish intelligence coordinator Stanislaw Zaryn viewed the talks as an attempt to buy time and weaken the West ahead of another confrontation.

Published: 16:37 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 16:38 EST, 26 November 2026.

Wouter Vrancken claimed that Monaco’s 94th-minute winner at Tynecastle has not significantly diminished Hearts’ chances of reaching the knockout phase of the UEFA Conference League.

Vrancken’s team were left sickened when Folarin Balogun’s goal settled a thrilling contest in stoppage time to condemn them to a third consecutive defeat in the league phase of the competition after their away losses to Trabzonspor and Thun.

Hearts, who have just one point from their opening night draw at home to Nordsjaelland, now have to win both of their remaining games – at home to Bosnian side Borac on December 10 and away to Pafos in Cyprus a week later – to have any chance of further progress.

‘I don’t think losing that point makes a difference,’ insisted Vrancken. ‘The pleasing thing for me was that at 2-2 we still wanted to go and try to win the game.

‘Three points would have made a difference — zero or one point tonight doesn’t make a difference towards the next two games. We have to win them both now, so that doesn’t change.’.

Vrancken took pride from Hearts’ display against their Ligue 1 opponents as two spectacular strikes from Jordi Altena and Sabah Kerjota cancelled out a Balogun penalty and Edan Diop’s goal in a breathless first half.

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken consoles goalscorer Sabah Kerjota as he is substituted.

While Balogun’s late winner was harsh on Hearts, Vrancken believes his players paid the price for poor game management and was critical of the contribution of subs Josh McPake, Finlay Pollock and James Wilson who came on in the closing stages of the game.

‘It did feel cruel but at the same time we have to learn from that situation,’ stated Vrancken. ‘Until then, we were really solid in not giving chances away.

‘I expect more from the guys who came on. We can win the ball with fresh players or make a foul somewhere to keep the result. I expect that kind of battling for the team, so we can do better there.

‘But the biggest thing is the performance we put on the park tonight against a really good side, knowing that we still have nine injuries and still do that against them. I’m really proud of them.

Sources indicate that ‘The goals we scored were really good and you see the confidence those guys have. They have taken confidence from the dynamics of what we did against Dundee at the weekend. The conviction in both boxes was there tonight and that’s notable for us to take into the next run of games.’.

Vrancken had no real complaint with Monaco’s penalty, awarded for a foul by Jamie McCart on Matthis Abline, but was unhappy that German referee Daniel Schlager failed to spot a foul on Kerjota before the visitors’ second goal.

Hearts players revel in the celebrations after Kerjota's wondergoal sent Tynecastle wild.

Recent findings suggest that ‘For me, the penalty was light but okay,’ added the Belgian. ‘But if you are really decisive to give a penalty there, then you don’t see one of our players having his shirt pulled in the build-up to their second goal, that’s frustrating.

‘At this level, things can happen like this. It wasn’t given for us and it wasn’t the only decision like that tonight.’.

Monaco coach Filipe Luis revelled in his team’s late win but admitted even he felt like joining in the acclamation of Kerjota’s goal for Hearts.

Sources indicate that ‘Hearts were a tough opponent and I knew it would be difficult,’ noted Luis. ‘We found spaces and created chances from the start but Hearts scored a fantastic goal to go ahead.

‘But we stayed calm and scored twice before they scored another fantastic goal. It was so good, I almost had to applaud it!

‘Hearts didn’t create many chances in the second half and in the end we managed to win, so there are many good things for us tonight.’.

Talk about cramming everything in. Brian Brobbey only played for 67 minutes but, in that time, he collected a yellow card, ripped Levi Colwill’s shirt and earned himself a standing ovation after morphing into a battering ram.

Sources indicate that régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s head coach, said there was nobody like the Netherlands striker in the Premier League and it said everything that everyone wanted to make Brobbey centre of attention after a long overdue home win, even though he had not scored. Everyone, that is, bar Xabi Alonso.

“No, he’s not unstoppable,” Chelsea’s head coach replied when asked why his team had found Brobbey too much to handle. “He’s stoppable – but only when you defend better than we did. We were not bullied. We didn’t produce enough.”.

That is one way of putting it. Another would be to say Brobbey was everything that Chelsea, much to Alonso’s disgust, were not: a bristling menace, a steamroller wearing a pair of boots, a player on a mission to help transform the mood – Enzo Le Fée’s decisive spot kick owed everything to Brobbey.

Chelsea arrived on Wearside looking to establish themselves in the top four ahead of the break but, instead, Alonso watched through his fingers as Sunderland reminded everyone why they were the joyous story of last season, a beautiful mix of inspiration and perspiration.

In fairness to the Chelsea manager, he refused to get caught in the minutiae of contentious penalty decisions – one that Chelsea were denied, another that they conceded – and could only lament as Sunderland ground out their first Premier League win since August 30, 70 long days ago.

“It wasn’t the best game,” Alonso said. “I think that we didn’t deserve more than probably one point, maybe. We need to be more consistent on the move, to get the ball from one side to the other, and we didn’t do that good enough. We didn’t produce enough to deserve to win.”.

Unlike Sunderland. If you had turned up at the Stadium of Light without looking at the Premier League table, you would not have believed the hosts were bottom and you would not have given credence to the idea Le Bris, who has worked miracles these past two years, was under pressure.

Industry observers note that things, however, could not have started worse for Le Bris. Though Granit Xhaka has not shown last season’s form in these challenging opening months, the game proposal was built around him, so to see the Sunderland captain hobbling off after three minutes was symptomatic of how things have gone for the Wearsiders.

Sources indicate that “He felt something in the final sprint of the warm-up,” Le Bris explained. “We don’t know how bad it is.”.

According to recent reports, he is not the kind of coach, though, who will bemoan bad fortune. Le Bris sent on Jules Ahoka to replace Xhaka and watched as he, along with colleagues in red and white, set about trampling all over Chelsea’s intentions with incessant hard work.

Yet there was more to it. Sunderland can play, either intricately or directly, and a lovely move in the 12th minute needed a desperate, sliding intervention from Pep Chavarría’s to stop Trai Hume’s volley sliding in at the far post.

In the next attack, another Chemsdine Talbi cross – the Moroccan having been found by a peach of a pass from goalkeeper Robin Roefs – invited Brobbey to inflict maximum damage, but the Dutchman made a hash of his opportunity.

The momentum could have changed completely in the 23rd minute. Alonso, his players and staff were convinced they would be given a penalty after Cole Palmer tumbled when his legs tangled with Luke O’Nien but, after a lengthy delay, VAR Nick Hopton felt there was no case to answer.

Industry observers note that hopton was involved again in the 33rd minute but, as Alonso said, Chelsea only had themselves to blame. Colwill simply could not contain Brobbey when he began marauding, grappling, grabbing and clipping the Dutchman’s heels. Le Fée did the rest, sending Mike Penders the wrong way.

Recent findings suggest that from that point, Chelsea were in trouble, no matter how many changes Alonso made. They huffed, puffed, but nothing worked. They had come up against a red-and-white wall, fortified by constant backing from the stands, and the west Londoners were never going to knock it down.

Sources indicate that one incident, as the clock ticked towards 90 minutes, encapsulated everything good about this Sunderland display when O’Nien chased down substitute Geovany Quenda to make a challenge. Another moment of defending from Thomas Meunier on Morgan Rogers was exceptional.

Recent findings suggest that “You could see our identity and our togetherness and the way we managed the game,” noted Le Bris, who was booked when hectoring referee Jarred Gillett. “These three points were critical. It was a struggle at times to manage situations. We revealed as a group real heart.”.

And nobody did that more than Brobbey. No wonder Le Bris will be hoping Xavi Hernández, the Netherlands head coach, handles him with care over the next 10 days. On this form, he will be the fuel that drives Sunderland’s quest for survival.

In a recent development, “You know when you come here in this stadium it will be a difficult game and that was the matter tonight. We knew it would be tough, we are disappointed we lost the game. At one point it went very fast from side to side. Sometimes we had to control. With 11 behind the ball it is difficult to find the spaces.”.

On where Chelsea stand ahead of the international break...

According to recent reports, “How you do – good or not – it is a matter of staying together. The international break is coming so the lads can be calm in the head and when we all come back we need to be motivated to go again.”.

Today is must-win match: for both sides.

For Sunderland that argument is easy to make – they are bottom of the Premier League, are without a win since August and for morale, if nothing else need at least a point, though three is really what the doctor orders.

For Chelsea – fourth in the table and with three wins in their past four league outings – the argument that this is a must-win game is harder to make, but bear with me here...

Facing a Sunderland team who are suffering from the worst of both worlds – blunt in attack and pitiful in defence (what a difference from last season...) and have proven all too easy to beat (as their 2-0 home defeat Zagreb illustrated on Thursday) – the west Londoners are expected to win. Fail to return to the capital with the three points and there will once again be question marks over Xabi Alonso’s side. They are flaky and flashy in equal measure, able to play and win well in spurts, but once again unable to mount sustained pressure needed for a title challenge and forced to battle it out for the hope of a top-four spot at best. Those will be the arguments raised should they not win this afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that the hosts doubtless wish that their ‘issues’ were as golden as today’s opposition. For Trai Hume, who scored in this fixture last season, the Sunderland players are at fault for the sorry start to the season and he wants to put right the wrongs so far, starting today.

“I couldn’t tell you what’s changed. We thought we’d addressed it after the Leeds game, where we were aggressive, strong, but we go out there tonight and see the old habits of the start of the season. Everything’s a bit laboured, and it’s something the staff can’t fix, it’s on us as players,” Hume stated.

“We’re still together as a club, as a team. I think the run of form we’re on, it would be easy to think we’re not, but we are. We are really upset with how we’ve been playing, and the results don’t lie. We haven’t been good enough and we know that. We have to address that.”.

Amorim: ‘Hutchinson changed the game more than me’ as Ramos injury concern emerges for Milan

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim believes Milan’s comeback win over Olympiacos could be “the start of something”, but warned that his side still have plenty of work to do.

Sources indicate that with quotes via MilanNews.it, the Milan coach was speaking to Sky Sport Italia and at his press conference after the Rossoneri came from 2-0 down to win 4-2 in Piraeus. Omari Hutchinson scored one goal and set up two more.

“It definitely changes our future. We did well in the second half, but we made a lot of mistakes again and we have to improve,” Amorim said. “We have a lot to do to become a very strong team, but the spirit is there. This is the start of something.”.

In a recent development, the result gives Milan’s Europa League campaign a lifeline. They had won just one of their first four league-phase games, beating Salzburg, before tonight’s victory moved them on to six points.

Sources indicate that “To believe it, you have to see it,” Amorim added. “Today we saw that we came back from two goals down and won 4-2. Our confidence will grow.”.

Amorim insisted Hutchinson’s display wasn’t a surprise.

It has been revealed that “I always expect this from him. He has the potential to do much more. He has talent, like other players in the squad, but it’s the head that counts,” he said.

He also played down his own role, despite the impact of his substitutes.

Industry observers note that “I didn’t change the game. Ramos came off because he was in pain, so it was a normal substitution. Hutchinson changed the game more than I did. What changed it was the first goal,” he said.

Industry observers note that that will be a concern for Milan. Gonçalo Ramos was also taken off as a precaution with thigh pain in Sunday’s win over Frosinone, and the Rossoneri travel to Cagliari on Monday.

Amorim was also critical of his side’s first-half build-up play, singling out Koni De Winter, who was replaced eight minutes after the break.

Sources indicate that “We lost the ball without being under pressure. Koni sometimes put the ball into areas where there was pressure, when he should have carried it. He’s responsible for pushing the team up and leading us out.”.

Fikayo Tomori, who replaced De Winter, earned praise, and Amorim admitted he had changed his mind about the defender since the start of the season.

“He has speed, which was vital today, and he has experience. He can improve a lot. I’ve changed my mind compared to the start of the season, and I’m grateful for that.”.

Amorim then apologised for Diego Moreira’s celebration after the fourth goal.

Industry observers note that “It won’t happen again. Moreira is a young lad who plays, but he has to grow. We know we wouldn’t like it if they did that to our fans. It’s my responsibility, and I apologise, but he didn’t do it with bad intent.”.

Industry News: Hashim Thaci's second conviction in The Hague reignites debate in Kosovo about justice and the Kosovo Specialist Chambers

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A court in The Hague on Tuesday convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of obstructing justice and attempting to influence witnesses during his recent war crimes trial and sentenced him to 17 months in prison.
  • This term will be added to his 25-year sentence for war crimes, which was handed down by the same court, the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, on September 16.
  • According to the indictment of the Specialist Prosecutor's Office, Thaci had provided visitors at the detention facility in The Hague with confidential information about witnesses in his war crimes trial and had instructed them on how to influence their testimony.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A court in The Hague on Tuesday convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of obstructing justice and attempting to influence witnesses during his recent war crimes trial and sentenced him to 17 months in prison.

This term will be added to his 25-year sentence for war crimes, which was handed down by the same court, the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, on September 16.

According to the indictment of the Specialist Prosecutor's Office, Thaci had provided visitors at the detention facility in The Hague with confidential information about witnesses in his war crimes trial and had instructed them on how to influence their testimony.

Three other men — former head of the Kosovo Intelligence Agency Bashkim Smakaj, former Minister of Justice Hajredin Kuci, and Fadil Fazliu — were also convicted.

In a recent development, thaci, who was the former political leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) during the 1998-1999 Kosovo War, is viewed by many in his home country as a hero. His war crimes conviction in September was greeted in Kosovo with anger and dismay.

Thaci has vowed to appeal the war crimes conviction.

His two convictions touch deep sensitivities in Kosovo society. Tuesday's ruling brings renewed attention to the war that ended 27 years ago, the role played by its former leaders, and the continuing debate over justice, individual or collective responsibility for the KLA's war to liberate Kosovo from Serbia, and trust in judicial institutions.

The response from the government of Kosovo was swift.

It has been revealed that in a statement issued on Tuesday, the government said, "Trust in justice is built not only on the decisions that are made, but also on the manner in which they are reached. Therefore, our commitment to the rule of law and our insistence on the full respect of rights and procedural guarantees are part of the same principled position: Justice must not only be done, but must also be fair, transparent, and credible.".

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers was established in 2015 by the parliament of Kosovo at the instigation of the European Union and the United States.

The court was created to investigate serious crimes allegedly committed by members of the KLA during and after the Kosovo War.

For security reasons, including concerns about witness intimidation, the court was located in The Hague in the Netherlands.

After Thaci and three others were convicted of war crimes in first instance in September, Kosovo's state authorities established a working group to draft a strategy regarding the appeal proceedings before the Kosovo Specialist Chambers.

The group is chaired by Foreign Minister Glauk Konjufca and includes members of Kosovo's parliament.

Prime Minister Albin Kurti has stated that the working group continues to believe that "the first-instance judgment of the Specialist Chambers is unjust, both legally and morally," and that as a result, "the government is working to secure a correction at the appeals level before the Specialist Chambers.".

In addition, the parliament of Kosovo is presently considering amendments to the law governing the Kosovo Specialist Chambers.

The draft law, which is expected to be adopted, envisages narrowing the court's mandate in several areas, including the time period covered by its jurisdiction, limiting the maximum prison sentence to 15 years, allowing sentences to be served in Kosovo, and introducing the possibility of presidential pardons for persons convicted by final court decisions.

How do political analysts and legal experts view the parliament's attempt to amend the law on the Kosovo Specialist Chambers before the judicial process involving the four men convicted of war crimes has reached a final verdict?

"From an international perspective, at first glance, this initiative could even be interpreted as an attempt to interfere in the judicial process," said political analyst and university professor Artan Muhaxheri.

"Precisely for this reason, it is essential that Kosovo's political spectrum and its legal experts demonstrate beyond any doubt that this measure does not conflict with Kosovo's international obligations toward the European Union," Muhaxheri told DW, adding that this is the only way to ensure that the desired outcome is achieved and that the initiative does not produce the opposite effect.

"Issues relating to jurisdiction, statutory limits on maximum sentences, and other similar matters must be argued professionally and rigorously, demonstrating that they fully guarantee judicial independence and enjoy solid support within Kosovo's legal system, the same legal system that, first and foremost, established the Specialist Chambers," he said.

Ehat Miftaraj, executive director of the Kosovo Law Institute (IKD), told DW that although the Kosovo Specialist Chambers were established by the Republic of Kosovo itself, "the way the judicial process has unfolded has created the impression that judges, prosecutors and certain international actors have treated not only the accused but also Kosovo itself with distrust, prejudice, and an often condescending approach.".

Miftaraj went on to say that reactions and objections in Kosovo to the decisions of the Specialist Chambers are also interpreted and judged in the historical and emotional context of the war and what Kosovo's citizens experienced during and after it.

Sources indicate that "In a democratic society, every citizen, including political and institutional representatives, has the right to criticize judicial decisions," he stated. "However, there is a fundamental distinction between criticism based on legal arguments and attempts to delegitimize courts or exert influence over judicial proceedings. And here, there is room for criticism of both sides.".

England Under-21s manager Lee Carsley has told GIVEMESPORT that nothing has changed regarding Archie Gray’s international situation amid interest from Scotland, while backing Jobe Bellingham to have a ‘massive future’ with the Three Lions.

England were drawn in Group A alongside France, Poland and co-hosts Serbia for next summer’s European Championship on Thursday evening, with Carsley’s side looking to win the competition for a third consecutive time.

Having overseen successive European Championship triumphs in 2023 and 2025, Carsley has an opportunity to further cement his legacy within England’s youth setup.

The 52-year-old spoke to GIVEMESPORT following the draw in Belgrade, discussing the international futures of several of England’s brightest young talents, including Gray, Bellingham, Max Dowman and Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven.

Gray’s international future has been a talking point amid interest from Scotland, with the Tottenham Hotspur midfielder eligible to represent both nations.

Carsley previously revealed that he had held conversations with Gray regarding the situation, but the England Under-21s boss insists nothing has changed since those discussions.

Speaking to GIVEMESPORT, Carsley remarked:.

“Archie, like a lot of the players, is key to the Under-21s. He’s got a fantastic history in the pathway, a player that we really enjoy working with.

“There’s no change to what we spoke about previously.”.

Gray’s versatility makes him a valuable asset within England’s youth setup, although competition for places in Thomas Tuchel’s senior squad remains fierce.

One player who has already been rewarded with a senior international opportunity is Jobe Bellingham.

Having worked closely with the midfielder at Under-21 level, Carsley believes Bellingham was fully deserving of his opportunity and expects him to feature in the senior setup again in the future.

“I think it’s always difficult to get into that senior squad. Having been there myself, I realise how difficult it is to pick a squad.

“Jobe more than deserved his opportunity. I imagine he’ll be there in the future.

“He’s a really crucial player for us, a player that I love working with. He’s got a massive future with England. He deserves all the applause that he gets.”.

Few young English players have generated as much excitement as Arsenal youngster Max Dowman.

The teenager made history during the November international break, breaking Jude Bellingham’s record to become England’s youngest-ever Under-21 goalscorer with his winner against France.

Despite his age, Carsley believes Dowman has already demonstrated that he belongs at Under-21 level and is relishing the opportunity to play a role in his development.

Sources indicate that “I think he revealed last camp that he was more than capable of being there. He’s an outstanding talent on and off the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that “Great player to work with. Lovely kid as well also, which is really vital. Settled into the group nicely.

“Max is a player that we rate highly.”.

Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven has previously spent time training with Carsley’s Under-21 group and could be among those competing for a place in next summer’s squad.

Asked specifically about Heaven’s prospects of featuring at the European Championship, Carsley revealed he is monitoring approximately 65 players before selecting his final 23-man squad.

“I think there’s a lot of players that are potentially in and around that squad. I’m watching maybe 65 players in total to pick 23.

“We’ve also got our Under-20s and our Under-19s as well, who are a very strong age group.

“We just have to make sure that our squad is very competitive. It has to be a difficult squad to get into, but also to stay in that squad. It’s got to be a challenge as well.”.

Ethan Nwaneri and Mikey Moore have both taken the opportunity to continue their development away from English football this season.

While Carsley stopped short of encouraging more young English players to move abroad, he believes both youngsters have benefited from stepping outside their comfort zones.

It has been revealed that “I definitely wouldn’t encourage players. I think every player’s got an individual path that they have to go on.

“The two players that you’ve mentioned there, I think it’s really helped their development to move away from home and their comfort of being at home, to learn another language, to play another style of play.

“I was really impressed with Mikey on the last camp, as I was with Ethan.”.

Despite being handed a challenging group featuring France, Poland and co-hosts Serbia, Carsley insists England’s expectations have not changed following their successive European Championship triumphs.

The former England interim manager believes his players have a unique opportunity to create their own legacy next summer.

“I think you come to terms when you’re an England coach that expectation is very high every game, whether that’s a friendly or whether that’s a tournament.

“If you’re going to win a tournament, as we have done in the last two previous tournaments, you have to beat the best teams.”.

Asked about his excitement surrounding the next generation of English talent and the opportunity to win a third consecutive European Championship, Carsley added:.

“The players that I’m privileged to coach and work with and select have got a great opportunity now to make history of winning the tournament three times in a row in this format, and creating our own history and legacy within the Under-21s.

“To play a small part of that is something that we’re looking forward to.”.

Breaking: London’s people-first approach to smart-city development

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (874 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A virtual-reality model of London’s main financial district, the City of London, has mapped the size and location of every building.Credit: Mike Kemp/In Pictures via Getty Images.
  • London has risen to fourth place in the IMD Smart City Index 2026, up from sixth place in 2025 and eighth place in 2024.
  • In a recent development, “We increasingly describe our work as ‘city innovation’ rather than ‘smart cities’, because in many people’s minds ‘smart’ is associated with gadgets and gizmos,” states Dorling.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A virtual-reality model of London’s main financial district, the City of London, has mapped the size and location of every building.Credit: Mike Kemp/In Pictures via Getty Images.

London has risen to fourth place in the IMD Smart City Index 2026, up from sixth place in 2025 and eighth place in 2024. The index — which is published by IMD, an independent Swiss business institute — draws mostly on residents’ perceptions of infrastructure and technology, not a tally of sensors. That focus on perspective is key, notes Trevor Dorling, managing director of DG Cities, a private urban-innovation consultancy spun out of the Royal Borough of Greenwich local authority, which works to make better use of data and introduce latest technologies in the southeast London borough.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

In a recent development, “We increasingly describe our work as ‘city innovation’ rather than ‘smart cities’, because in many people’s minds ‘smart’ is associated with gadgets and gizmos,” states Dorling. “The aim is to use technology to create better places for people. It shouldn’t be the technologists who define what ‘better’ is, but the communities that live there.”.

There is plenty of evidence that London has the resources and knowledge to apply research solutions in such a people-centred way. In the 2026 Nature Index Science Cities table, London is ranked 21st overall, but it jumps to 5th place for health-sciences output, for instance.

The Smart Mobility Living Lab, created by a consortium of public and private organizations, including DG Cities, spans 24 kilometres of roads in Greenwich and the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park in Stratford, and is one example of London’s efforts to create societal impact with its innovation.

Sources indicate that the area has more than 1,000 different road features, from speed bumps and pedestrian crossings to one-way systems and bridges, that allow companies to test fresh vehicles and services in busy, real-world complexity. “The driving force for this was the rapid development of self-driving technologies and exploring the opportunities this presented for safety and accessibility, as well as the challenges,” indicates Dorling.

Trials to test self-driving shuttle buses and delivery vans have put the technology in public view, with residents invited to ride in the test vehicles, an openness that Dorling says has helped overcome scepticism and brought local authorities into the development process at an early stage.

London’s digital-twin projects are similarly pragmatic. The local authority in Harrow (northwest London) uses high-resolution drone imagery to inspect and measure roofs and buildings remotely and to build interactive maps of parks. The council used this approach in April 2026 to make a 3D model of Headstone Manor and Museum — a restored medieval complex and local-history museum — saving £12,000 (US$16,260) by avoiding a conventional roof survey with scaffolding and manual inspections.

In London’s main financial district, known as the City of London, a virtual-reality model created by the local authority in collaboration with researchers and digital spatial mappers has captured the size and location of every building, window, lamppost and traffic light within the area to within two centimetres of accuracy, allowing planners and the public to properly scrutinize building proposals.

Elsa Arcaute, a complexity science researcher at University College London, cautions against too much faith in digital twins, as a city with all its complexity and interplay between urbanity, nature and human behaviour cannot be completely duplicated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Omari Hutchinson, Christian Pulisic and Alphadjo Cissè have all reacted to Milan’s comeback win over Olympiacos, with Pulisic warning that every game is now a final.

With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb and MilanNews.it, the trio spoke to Sky Sport after the Rossoneri recovered from 2-0 down to win 4-2 in Piraeus, giving their Europa League campaign a vital boost.

It has been revealed that hutchinson was the star of the night. He started the fightback with a brilliant solo goal, set up Cissè and Pulisic, then broke from an Olympiacos corner to begin the move for Diego Moreira’s late fourth.

“I played in a slightly different position, then on the right I had much more space,” Hutchinson said. “I feel very comfortable here, there are a lot of players playing really well.

Industry observers note that “When I come in, I have to make an impact. It’s the same for me wherever I play, but right wing is the best position because I have more space. I’m adapting and enjoying it a lot.”.

Pulisic made the difference off the bench. He replaced Gonçalo Ramos at half-time, scored the winner and set up the fourth. According to our match report, that’s his fifth goal in his last six appearances.

“It was a decisive game for us. From today, every game is like a final,” the American stated. “We didn’t start well, but we were much better in the second half. It’s notable to find this intensity.

It has been revealed that “Hutchinson changed this game. I’m always there to help the team with whatever it needs.”.

Pulisic admitted Milan must stop making slow starts in Europe.

“I don’t have answers. It’s difficult. It’s not easy to play here, they played with a lot of energy. But you’re right, we have to get into games earlier, otherwise it’s not good enough.

Recent findings suggest that “We also have a newly introduced coach this year, and it takes some time to learn this system. I see a real team that sticks together. We’re all growing together.”.

Cissè’s header made it 2-2, and he put the team first.

“Scoring is always nice, but the win comes before everything,” he said.

Asked where he plays when Hutchinson is used behind the striker, he added: “He’s left-footed, I play on the left. Like the others, I’m available for whatever the coach needs.”.

Milan now turn their attention to Monday’s trip to Cagliari.

‘And of course, once again, Duran has done it. He is just a magnificent footballer.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill praised Camilo Duran for once again riding to the rescue.

‘Despite the fact that we’d plenty of possession, I thought that we should just accelerate once or twice, not only just into their half, but also be more penetrative,’ he added.

It has been revealed that ‘And I think that was the point. I thought we had a lot of ball in the second half as well.

‘There’s always a possibility on the break that you could concede but we had to take the chance because the three points tonight were of vital importance.

‘But, yeah, there’s lots that we can still do to improve our game.’.

Duran's downward header sealed the points for Celtic and ignited their qualification hopes.

The dramatic outcome ensured Celtic are now up to 25th place in the 36-team group – from 32nd – after losing their opening three matches.

O’Neill’s men next face Omonia with Marseille and Union Saint-Gilloise to come in January.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I’m just delighted to have won — it keeps us going,’ added O’Neill. ‘We’ve got six points on the board and we’ve still got a couple of games to go.

‘So, from an absolutely almost impossible position, having lost the first three games, we’ve given ourselves some hope.’.

Celtic’s star man on the night, Jota set up the opening goal and relished the return to his homeland almost two years after his last European match.

‘It’s been a long time that I wanted to come back to Portugal and play in front of my friends and family,’ he said. ‘And there’s no better way than with a win with three points. It was something that we wanted to achieve today and luckily we did it.

In a recent development, ‘It was a long road and I did my maximum to be as fit as possible. And right now it’s all about enjoying. There’s no expectation — just to be a professional, having the responsibility of being a Celtic player and delivering every day.’.

The Argentine manager is renowned for his demanding approach to physical conditioning, and there were already signs of his methods being implemented following the full-time whistle in Lisbon.

Several of United’s non-starters were spotted taking part in an additional weights session on the pitch at the Estádio José Alvalade immediately after the game.

Among those involved were Matthijs de Ligt, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount and Andrey Santos, with the players using dumbbells and other conditioning equipment.

Sources indicate that BBC Sports Live: “Some of Manchester United’s non-starters were out on the pitch doing a weights session after tonight’s game. Mauricio Pochettino must feel that fitness has an notable part to play if performances are to improve.”.

Despite suffering a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in Pochettino’s first game in charge on Sunday, there were considerably more encouraging signs from United against Sporting.

The Red Devils looked sharper going forward, particularly after the interval, when Pochettino reportedly demanded greater aggression and more forward runs from his players.

Bruno Fernandes responded by scoring twice in the space of three minutes against his former club.

The Portuguese international converted a 48th-minute penalty before producing a delightful lob over Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira in the 50th minute to turn the game on its head.

United’s attacking movement and willingness to commit players forward offered an encouraging glimpse of what Pochettino could bring to the team with more time on the training ground.

Ultimately, United were left wondering how they did not leave Portugal with all three points.

After Senne Lammens spilled a routine 80th-minute cross to gift Luis Suárez a second equaliser, United thought they had snatched an 83rd-minute winner when Kaique Pereira flapped Fernandes’ corner into his own net, only for VAR to controversially rule it out for a soft foul by Patrick Dorgu on the goalkeeper.

Combined with Youri Tielemans’ harsh stoppage-time second yellow card, Pochettino’s side were deeply unfortunate not to celebrate their first victory of the newly introduced era.

Sean Dyche enjoyed a fine playing career as a footballer, spending time with Nottingham Forest, Watford, Millwall, and Chesterfield, but he is best known for his time as a manager at the top level.

The Englishman has taken charge of 521 games during his managerial career, with spells at Watford, Burnley, Everton, and Nottingham Forest across the Championship and Premier League.

350 of those games have come in the top flight, which has seen the 55-year-old be able to manage some top players, who have represented their countries and gone on to play at the very highest level.

Playing at the top level, Dyche has coached some top stars such as Kieran Trippier, Morgan Gibbs-White, Ashley Young, Seamus Coleman, and Elliot Anderson.

But while speaking exclusively to GIVEMESPORT, via BetSelect.co.uk, the coach known for his strong defensive style of football was asked who the most underrated player of his coaching career was up to this point, and his response was surprising.

“You know what, the thing is, when I was manager at Burnley in particular, there’s so many of them," he mentioned.

According to recent reports, "I mean, the first three players I signed at Burnley – I always reference them because we signed them on free transfers. We didn’t have any money, or no real money.

It has been revealed that "I brought in Scott Arfield, Tom Heaton, and Dave Jones, all on free transfers. There’s three straight off the bat. But there’ve been so many who, not necessarily underrated, but like unsung heroes. So I wouldn’t say underrated. There’s not many I’ve worked with who I think were disrespected by being underrated. I think it was more, they’re a bit more under the radar: good club players, but top pros.

"So there are three that jump off the page, mainly because those three made such a difference to the side, and yet they were three free transfers, and we got promoted that season to the Premier League.

"So I look back at that and think, well, there’s certainly three players straight away – but like I say, I must reiterate it, not necessarily underrated in a disrespectful way, more that you didn’t realise how good they were until you worked with them.”.

According to recent reports, heaton spent six years at Burnley working under Dyche, but his career is one that would be considered to be great for any professional. He came through the academy at Manchester United and spent a number of years out on loan, before a spell with Cardiff and Bristol City prior to joining Burnley.

Sources indicate that he then went on to play for Aston Villa, and has since returned to Man Utd in the latter years of his career, working as the third-choice shot-stopper. He also earned three caps for England.

Arfield, meanwhile, spent five years at Turf Moor working with Dyche before joining Rangers, and becoming part of the squad that won the Scottish Premiership, Scottish Cup, and reached the Europa League final.

Dave Jones joined the club at 29 and was closer to the end of his career, and spent three years with the club before moving on to Sheffield Wednesday and ending his career at Wrexham.

None of the three players were ever really considered to be top-level stars, and it makes sense that Dyche names them as being underrated. But they were all hugely crucial to his time at Burnley, in particular, and it's clear that they made a big impression on him.

#141306. How a green economy could help reverse climate change

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1442 w)

How a green economy could help reverse climate change

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1442 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Human civilization is presently profoundly unsustainable.
  • If economies and societies keep to business as usual, the Earth's vital processes will continue to be thrown wildly out of balance, threatening the future of humanity.
  • It's now largely accepted that if humans are to have any chance of slowing global warming and nature loss, those social and economic models must change.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Human civilization is presently profoundly unsustainable. Earth has already crossed seven of the nine planetary boundaries critical for sustaining life, including climate change, ocean acidification and biosphere integrity.

If economies and societies keep to business as usual, the Earth's vital processes will continue to be thrown wildly out of balance, threatening the future of humanity.

It's now largely accepted that if humans are to have any chance of slowing global warming and nature loss, those social and economic models must change. That's where the idea of green growth comes in.

Its promise is to keep growing the economy while reducing emissions and resource use. That involves, for instance, running factories, businesses and homes on wind, solar and other green energy instead of coal and gas, replacing gas-fired furnaces with heat pumps and  recycling and reusing resources and raw materials.

Sources indicate that "Basically, the idea is: business as usual, but with more sustainable technologies," mentioned Helmut Haberl, a social ecology professor at BOKU University in Vienna. Along with his colleagues, he published a major report in 2020 evaluating more than 800 studies on green growth.

In principle, the world's economic output could continue to grow in the long term and generate significantly fewer emissions from the burning of fossil fuels like coal, oil and gas. That's been shown in scenarios modeled by researchers with the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, or IPCC.

Thanks to renewable energy and green technologies, those scenarios have already become reality in several countries and regions.

Recent findings suggest that the economies of developed countries like the United Kingdom, the United States, Japanand Australia have experienced years of growth alongside sinking CO2 emissions. That's even when offshore production is included.

According to recent reports, in the European Union, the bloc-wide economy has grown by more than 70% since 1990. Meanwhile, the EU's carbon emissions have dropped by around 40%.

But such a complete decoupling of growth and emissions is, according to Haberl and his fellow researchers, relatively rare.

Recent findings suggest that in India, and in several countries in Africa and Southeast Asia, economies are becoming more efficient. But while economic performance is outpacing emissions growth, emissions are still rising in those countries and globally. This is not compatible with preventing the worst impacts of climate change.

"That doesn't mean, however, that it couldn't work in the future," noted Haberl, referring to decoupling of growth and emissions.

And even though economic growth has been shown to be compatible with emissions reduction, eliminating all greenhouse gases from a polluting industry like steel or chemicals is complicated.

These sectors don't just release emissions by burning fossil fuels for energy; carbon is also a key part of the chemical processes used to create their products, notably in the steel industry.

Replacing it with greener substitutes, or an alternative energy source like green hydrogen, requires significant investment.

There's another hurdle: the world's high consumption of resources. A productive economy depends on many raw materials and other products: ores, chemicals, wood, cement, glass and agricultural products.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Many countries are now using green technologies to reduce the amount of resources needed to manufacture a product, for example, and are making their economies more efficient.

But that doesn't mean overall fewer resources are being used because falling costs can encourage businesses to produce more things and people to consume more. This can partially offset green savings and is called the rebound effect.

The British economy has been growing for years, emissions have been dropping and efficiency has increased, but the UK still used 7% more resources in 2023 than it did in 2001.

Sources indicate that global resource consumption has tripled over the last 50 years. If the world continues on the current pathway, that could increase by another 60% by 2060. It remains unclear whether green growth can deliver the emissions and resource reductions needed to stop climate change and biodiversity loss rapidly enough.

"We really need to move beyond efficiency gains in our existing production practices to look more broadly at what we consume," remarked Catherine Ganzleben, a sustainability and fair transitions expert at the European Environment Agency.

She told DW that people also need to reconsider how they consume and whether they really need to own everything they use in their daily life — cars, for example.

"But we can shift towards models where we share cars, so we pool our resources and have significantly lower resources per person through sharing the goods that we need.".

Some researchers have concluded that unrestricted economic growth is no longer possible in the long term, even if it's sustainable.

Recent findings suggest that instead, they've called for degrowth. This posits slower economic growth, no growth at all or even negative growth, so that the world's ecosystems and the climate have a chance to recover and stabilize.

It has been revealed that that applies mainly to economies in richer countries, which would need to take targeted steps to reduce their energy and resource use. Poorer countries would continue to grow until their economies and quality of life improve significantly.

In a recent development, under the degrowth theory, a society's prosperity is not measured solely by the growth of its gross domestic product, but by values such as quality of life, education and community. The idea is that once countries develop to a certain point, additional growth doesn't translate into greater well-being.

According to recent reports, ultimately, the concept is based on the idea that human well-being and ecological sustainability is only possible in the long term with a planned, socially just reduction of material production and resource consumption. Degrowth advocates argue this would be preferable to an unplanned and potentially catastrophic economic contraction caused by escalating climate extremes.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A 2020 study by researchers from the universities of Leeds and Lausanne showed that the concept of degrowth supported the world's climate goals — and that a high quality of life didn't have to be sacrificed in exchange for a significantly lower consumption of energy and resources.

However, there is still no conclusive evidence that an entire modern economy could continue to function entirely on the degrowth principles in the long term.

Nevertheless, Haberl doesn't assume that an environmentally friendly economic model automatically goes hand in hand with sacrifice, arguing instead for a needs-based economy.

"A society isn't necessarily better off when it's producing more goods and services," he stated. It all depends on how prosperity and quality of life are measured in the future, and how states decide to do business.

According to recent reports, today, a successful economy is measured by the growth of a country's gross domestic product — put simply, the worth of all of its goods and services. This calculation doesn't account for income distribution, unpaid work, quality of life or environmental damage.

It has been revealed that "The highest possible real incomes for every individual would probably not be compatible with ecological goals in the long term," said Haberl. "On the other hand, an increase in prosperity — related to a higher quality of life — would be.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

An analysis by the European Environment Agency (EEA) pointed out that the idea of steady growth is part of the world's economic cycle, and deeply anchored in our institutions, norms and societal discourse. The job market and tax system are also closely tied to gross domestic product growth. A shrinking economy would therefore require a fundamental shift in our way of thinking.

Countries face a dilemma: a steadily growing economy is not compatible with ecological goals, according to the EEA. On the other side, a sharp decline in growth could trigger enormous social upheaval.

According to recent reports, and the correlation is much more complex than the idea of "less is more," as highlighted by an EEA study in November 2021. "The fact that GDP growth has been harmful for the environment does not necessarily mean that declining GDP would be good for the environment," noted the report.

According to recent reports, achieving green growth while respecting environmental limits would require an "unprecedented decoupling of economic activity from environmental and climate pressures. Whether this is feasible is right now uncertain.".

This article was originally written in German.

Juventus recovered from a Neto howler to beat Omonia Nicosia 4-1 with Jeff Ekhator, Andrea Cambiaso, Jeremie Boga and Francisco Conceicao on target.

The Bianconeri won three of their first four Europa League games, plus a 2-2 with Stade Rennais, but were missing Pierre Kalulu, Nico Gonzalez, Kerim Alajbegovic, Khephren Thuram, Manuel Locatelli, Arek Milik and Kamil Grabara, while Edon Zhegrova and Daniele Rugani are not on the UEFA list. Neto got his first Juve appearance since May 2017, with Francisco Conceicao’s return after a shoulder injury on October 18.

Omonia had Fotis Kitsos and Mihlali Mayambela injured, while Carel Eiting, Moses Odubajo, David Akintola and Giorgos Viktoros were cup-tied.

See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog.

Francisco Conceicao stung the goalkeeper’s gloves in the opening minutes, but Omonia Nicosia took the lead with their first chance thanks to a howler from Neto.

The goalkeeper was understandably rusty after not playing since last season, and flapped aimlessly at a Muamer Tankovic corner, allowing Lubomir Satka to nod in undisturbed at the back post.

Juve took a while to shake off the shock, Juan Cabal testing Thomas Kaminski from distance, yet Florin Tanase threatened a second by drilling wide from the edge of the area, as did Satka on a free kick, as the jeers started to rain down from the stands.

It needed something to wake them up, and it was provided by Andrea Cambiaso with a ferocious, swerving left-foot finish from distance into the far top corner.

There was almost a third moments later, as Conceicao pulled back from the by-line for Gatti’s angled drive, parried by Kaminski’s boot.
